definition_zh: 不安的；心神不宁的；不自在的；令人不安的；不稳定的
definition_en: slightly worried or uncomfortable, or making people feel that something is wrong
core_image: 坐在椅子上却怎么也找不到一个安稳的姿势
scene: 深夜的病房里，家人守着还没出结果的化验单，谁也坐不住。The silence in the waiting room made everyone uneasy.
sceneCN: 这里 uneasy 是「心神不宁的」（第 1 个义项：心里不踏实）；句意为候诊室里的沉默让每个人都坐立不安。找不到安稳姿势的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不安地；局促地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不安；局促」
去掉否定前缀 un- 后的肯定形式，义为「容易的；从容的」

senses.title: Feeling worried without a clear reason
senses.definition: slightly worried or nervous, often without being able to say why
senses.definitionCN: 有点担心或紧张，往往说不出具体缘由
senses.example: She felt uneasy about the phone call and could not sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那通电话感到不安，翻来覆去睡不着。
senses.why: The prefix means not, and the base word means at ease, so uneasy is literally not at ease.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「安逸、自在」，因此 uneasy 字面上就是「不自在」，不安从这里直接生出。

senses.title: Awkward in company
senses.definition: not comfortable in a social situation, as if you do not know what to do with yourself
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中不舒服，手脚都不知往哪里放
senses.example: He gave an uneasy laugh and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他局促地笑了一下，换了个话题。
senses.why: The same lack of ease that keeps the body restless also shows in a voice or a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 让身体坐立难安的那份不自在，同样会从嗓音和笑声里露出来。

senses.title: A silence or mood that suggests trouble
senses.definition: used of a silence, mood, or peace that seems to hide a problem
senses.definitionCN: 形容沉默、气氛或和平似乎掩盖着问题
senses.example: An uneasy silence fell over the table after his remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一句话之后，桌上一片令人不安的沉默。
senses.why: A feeling of not being at ease spreads from people to the room they sit in.
senses.whyCN: 不自在的感觉会从人传到人所在的屋子，于是空气本身也显得不安。

senses.title: A relationship or arrangement that may not last
senses.definition: used of a peace, alliance, or agreement that is forced and may break down
senses.definitionCN: 形容被迫达成、随时可能破裂的和平、联盟或协议
senses.example: The two sides reached an uneasy truce before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在入冬前达成了勉强的停战。
senses.why: Anything that leaves people not at ease is also likely to fall apart.
senses.whyCN: 任何让人无法安心的安排，往往也难以长久维持。

senses.title: Sleep that is broken and shallow
senses.definition: used of sleep that is light and full of waking moments
senses.definitionCN: 形容睡得浅、常常醒来的睡眠
senses.example: After a night of uneasy sleep she went back to the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 睡了一夜不踏实的觉，她又回到了医院。
senses.why: The body that cannot settle by day cannot settle at night either.
senses.whyCN: 白天找不到安稳姿势的身体，夜里同样安稳不下来。

intro.en: The word is a plain English construction: un- plus easy, with the mental sense of easy coming from Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是地道的英语构造：un- 加 easy，而 easy 的「安逸」之义来自古法语。

items.en: The prefix un- was already used to reverse the meaning of a word.
items.cn: 古英语时期，前缀 un- 已用于反转词义。

items.en: Aise meant comfort or leisure, and the phrase at ease entered English from it.
items.cn: aise 意为「舒适、闲暇」，短语 at ease 由此进入英语。

items.en: Ease and easy grew from that source and meant free from pain or trouble.
items.cn: ease 与 easy 由这一来源发展而来，意为「无痛无扰」。

items.en: Uneasy is formed by adding the negative prefix to easy and appears in writing in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: uneasy 由否定前缀加 easy 构成，十六世纪见于书面记录。

items.en: The sense widens to silences, alliances, and sleep, wherever a calm surface hides strain.
items.cn: 此后意义扩展到沉默、联盟与睡眠，只要平静的表面下藏着紧张就能用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other un- adjectives about attitude, while the near-meaning group collects words for fear.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他表示态度的 un- 形容词，近义组汇集表示担忧害怕的词。

entries.definition: not difficult, or free from worry
in a worried or awkward way

entries.definitionCN: 不稳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
不寻常的（只是前缀相同，词根不同）

normalIntro.en: Nothing in the word is exotic: a negative prefix rests on a word for comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词一点也不生僻：一个否定前缀压在一个表示舒适的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus easy: not at ease is exactly what uneasy means.
normal.cn: un- 加 easy：不在自在的状态，就是 uneasy 的本义。

normal.en: Feel uneasy about something is the most common frame for learners.
normal.cn: feel uneasy about 是学习者最常用的搭配框架。

normal.en: Uneasiness is the state, uneasily the manner of moving or speaking.
normal.cn: uneasiness 是那种状态，uneasily 是那种说话或动作的样子。

normal.en: An uneasy silence and an uneasy alliance both point to tension under the surface.
normal.cn: an uneasy silence 与 an uneasy alliance 都指向表面之下的紧张。

normal.en: Compare at ease, which means relaxed, to see the negative in action.
normal.cn: 对比 at ease（放松、自在）就能看清否定前缀的作用。

abstract.en: Picture hands on a chair arm, fingers tapping and stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手搭在椅臂上，手指敲了又停。

abstract.en: Hear a joke, then a laugh one beat too late.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话，然后是一声慢了半拍的笑。

abstract.en: Feel a room where everyone has decided not to say the obvious thing.
abstract.cn: 体会一个所有人都绕着明摆着的话说的房间。

examples.en: He was uneasy about leaving his mother alone in the house.
examples.cn: 他不放心把母亲一个人留在家里。

examples.en: An uneasy calm settled on the village after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，村子笼罩在一片令人不安的平静里。

examples.en: She smiled uneasily at the doctor and closed the door behind her.
examples.cn: 她对医生不安地笑笑，然后关上了身后的门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺意贼」——钱包里少了钱，俺心里就惦记着那个贼，坐也坐不稳。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ easy（安逸的），easy 义源自旧法语 aise（舒适、闲暇），短语 at ease 即由此而来

sensesIntro.en: A single state, not being at ease, spreads from the body to voices, rooms, agreements, and sleep.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份状态，不自在，从身体蔓延到嗓音、房间、协议与睡眠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that cannot find a settled position.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副怎么也摆不稳的身体。

branches.en: The private branch: a vague worry with no clear cause.
branches.cn: 私密分支：说不出缘由的隐约担忧。

branches.en: The social branch: the body that does not know how to stand.
branches.cn: 社交分支：身体不知该怎么摆。

branches.en: The atmosphere branch: a room that hints at a hidden problem.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：屋子暗示着藏起来的问题。

branches.en: The arrangement branch: a peace everyone expects to break.
branches.cn: 安排分支：人人都知道待不住的和平。

branches.en: The nightly branch: sleep that keeps coming apart.
branches.cn: 夜间分支：总是断开的睡眠。

intro.en: The word is built from a negative prefix and a borrowed adjective, so its parts are easy to read.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀与借入的形容词搭成，部件一眼可辨。

latinIntro.en: The base word is not Latin, but the Old French aise behind it may come from Latin adjacens, lying near.
latinIntro.cn: 词根本身不是拉丁语，但其后的旧法语 aise 可能源自拉丁语 adjacens（邻近的）。

items.example: Uneasy means not easy in comfort.
He glanced uneasily at the door.

items.exampleCN: 一种奇怪的不安充满了她。

definition_zh: 失业的；无业的；未被使用的；闲置的
definition_en: without a paid job, or not being put to use
core_image: 工作台上收起的工具，主人没有活可干
scene: 清晨的人才市场门口，几个中年人抱着简历站着，等一张招工的牌子。He has been unemployed since the factory closed.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployed 是「失业的」（第 1 个义项：没有工作）；句意为工厂关门以后他一直失业。收起工具、无活可干的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「失业；失业率」
去掉否定前缀的动词，义为「雇用；使用」
动词加 -ee 构成的施受名词，义为「雇员」
动词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「就业；雇用」

senses.title: Without a paid job
senses.definition: not having a job that brings in money, usually while still able to work
senses.definitionCN: 没有一份挣钱的工作，通常指仍有劳动能力的人
senses.example: Two thousand workers were left unemployed by the closure.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭让两千名工人失业。
senses.why: The prefix undoes the verb employ, so a person who is not employed is simply outside a job.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 把动词 employ（雇用）反转，不被雇用的人自然就落在工作之外。

senses.title: Registered as out of work
senses.definition: officially counted as looking for work and not currently having any
senses.definitionCN: 官方统计中算作正在找工作、目前没有工作的人
senses.example: He was unemployed for eight months before the interview call came.
senses.exampleCN: 他失业了八个月才等到面试通知。
senses.why: The same reversal takes on a statistical edge once governments count who is in and out of work.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始统计谁在岗谁不在岗，这份反转就有了统计上的含义。

senses.title: The group of people without work
senses.definition: used with the as a collective noun for all people out of work
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用作集合名词，指全体失业的人
senses.example: The city opened a centre to help the unemployed find training.
senses.exampleCN: 市里开设了一个中心，帮失业者寻找培训机会。
senses.why: An adjective applied to many people becomes a standing label for the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 一个形容词加在许多人身上，就成了指代整个群体的固定称呼。

senses.title: Tools or money not being used
senses.definition: used of machines, money, or skills that are available but not put to work
senses.definitionCN: 形容机器、资金或技能虽可用却未被投入使用
senses.example: The mill stood idle, its machinery unemployed for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那座磨坊停着，机器闲置了十年。
senses.why: If employ means to put to use, then anything not put to use is just as unemployed as a worker.
senses.whyCN: 既然 employ 也有「使用」之义，那么没有被使用的东西就和工人一样处于 unemployed 的状态。

senses.title: Time or energy going to waste
senses.definition: used figuratively of abilities or time that have no outlet
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地形容才能或时间无处发挥
senses.example: Her skills lay unemployed while she cared for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 照顾父亲的那几年，她的本事无处施展。
senses.why: The picture of a capable person outside work easily transfers to abilities outside use.
senses.whyCN: 一个有能力的人被挡在工作之外的画面，很容易挪到被闲置的才能上。

intro.en: Employ comes from Latin through French, and the negative adjective is a later English addition.
intro.cn: employ 经由法语来自拉丁语，带否定前缀的形容词则是后来英语自己加上的。

items.en: Implicare meant to enfold or involve, built from in- and plicare, to fold.
items.cn: implicare 意为「裹住、卷入」，由 in- 与 plicare（折叠）构成。

items.en: Emploier developed the sense of using something or someone for a purpose.
items.cn: emploier 发展出「为某目的使用某物或某人」的意思。

items.en: English took the verb as employ, first meaning to apply or use.
items.cn: 英语借入动词作 employ，最初意为「应用、使用」。

items.en: The sense of hiring someone for wages became the dominant one by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「付工资雇用」成为主要义项。

items.en: Un- was added to the past participle employed to describe those without work.
items.cn: 在过去分词 employed 前加 un-，用来指没有工作的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the employ family, while the near-meaning group gathers words about lacking a job.
note.cn: 形近组是 employ 词族，近义组汇集表示没有工作的词。

entries.definition: the state of having paid work
a person who is paid to work for others
a person or firm that pays others to work

entries.definitionCN: 未勘探的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: no longer needed for a job

normalIntro.en: The word is a verb with a lid on it: employ means to use or hire, un- takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被盖上否定盖子的动词：employ 是使用或雇用，un- 则把它拿走。

normal.en: Un- plus employed: not hired, not in use.
normal.cn: un- 加 employed：没被雇用，没被使用。

normal.en: The unemployed is a collective phrase and takes a plural verb sense in British use.
normal.cn: the unemployed 是集合说法，英式用法中带复数意味。

normal.en: Unemployment is the noun, and it is the word on news reports.
normal.cn: 名词是 unemployment，也是新闻里常见的词。

normal.en: Employ, employer, employee form a neat trio of verb, giver, receiver.
normal.cn: employ、employer、employee 组成动词、给方、受方的整齐三件套。

normal.en: Idle machinery and unemployed capital share the same logic of not being put to work.
normal.cn: 闲置的机器与闲着的资金，逻辑相同，都是没被投入使用。

abstract.en: Picture a factory gate at dawn with nobody walking in.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明的厂门口，没有人往里走。

abstract.en: See a toolbox closed on a bench, dust on the lid.
abstract.cn: 看工作台上合起的工具箱，盖子上落着灰。

abstract.en: Hear a phone that does not ring for weeks.
abstract.cn: 听一部几个星期不响的电话。

examples.en: She has been unemployed since the restaurant closed last spring.
examples.cn: 自去年春天餐馆关门后她就一直失业。

examples.en: The government promised new training for the unemployed.
examples.cn: 政府承诺为失业者提供新的培训。

examples.en: His years of experience sat unemployed while he looked after the children.
examples.cn: 照顾孩子的那几年，他的经验无处施展。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺木扑落的」——活儿没了，俺木头一样扑落在地上，闲着没事干。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ 过去分词 employed，employ 源自拉丁语 implicare（裹住、卷入），经古法语 emploier 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One reversal, not put to work, covers people, machines, money, and even talents.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次反转，「未被投入使用」，覆盖人、机器、资金乃至才能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tool box closed on a bench because there is no work to do.
core.cn: 核心意象：因为没活可干而合上的工具箱。

branches.en: The personal branch: the man at the gate and the figure in the statistics.
branches.cn: 个人分支：站在厂门口的人与统计表里的人。

branches.en: The collective branch: a phrase that names a whole group.
branches.cn: 集合分支：指称整个群体的固定说法。

branches.en: The equipment branch: machines and money standing still.
branches.cn: 器物分支：停着不动的机器和资金。

branches.en: The figurative branch: ability with nowhere to go.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：无处施展的本事。

branches.en: The plain description most learners meet first in the news.
branches.cn: 学习者最先在新闻里遇到的最朴素义项。

intro.en: The word is an English prefix on a French verb, so reading the parts is straightforward.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语前缀加法语动词，拆开看部件很直接。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb implicare lies behind the French form and supplies the oldest layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 implicare 藏在其后，是最早的一层。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词后缀
表示受事者的名词后缀

items.meaning: the state of having no job
having the worn look of the jobless
items.example: A shabby, unemployed-looking coat hung by the door.
items.exampleCN: 门边挂着一件像失业者穿的破旧外套。

definition_zh: 意外的；出乎意料的；没有料想到的；突兀的
definition_en: not anticipated or planned, so that it surprises people
core_image: 推开门发现屋里站着一位本以为还在远方的人
scene: 生日那天，灯一直关着，门后躲着一屋子的朋友，她一进门就叫出了声。Her visit was completely unexpected.
sceneCN: 这里 unexpected 是「意外的」（第 1 个义项：事先没有想到）；句意为她来访完全出乎意料。推门见人的画面就是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「意外地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「意外性」
去掉否定前缀与原后缀的动词，义为「期待；预料」
动词加 -ation 构成名词，义为「期待；预期」

senses.title: Not what anyone thought would happen
senses.definition: not believed likely to happen, so that it takes people by surprise
senses.definitionCN: 被认为不太会发生，因而让人吃惊
senses.example: Her answer was so unexpected that no one spoke for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答太出人意料，一时间谁都没说话。
senses.why: The prefix removes the verb of looking forward, so what is not looked forward to arrives without warning.
senses.whyCN: 前缀去掉了「向前张望」这个动作，没被张望的事物就毫无预告地到来了。

senses.title: A visit or arrival nobody planned for
senses.definition: used of a guest or arrival that no one had prepared for
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有人做过准备的客人或到来
senses.example: An unexpected visitor knocked just as dinner was served.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭刚端上桌，一位不速之客敲了门。
senses.why: The most visible kind of the unlooked-for is a person at the door.
senses.whyCN: 没被预料的种种事物中，最显眼的就是站在门口的那个人。

senses.title: An outcome that differs from the forecast
senses.definition: used of a result, turn, or ending that no one predicted
senses.definitionCN: 形容没人预测到的结果、转折或结局
senses.example: The trial took an unexpected turn on the second day.
senses.exampleCN: 审判第二天出现了意外的转折。
senses.why: Expect also means to predict, so a result that escapes prediction is unexpected.
senses.whyCN: expect 也有「预测」之义，逃出预测的结果自然就是意外的。

senses.title: Sudden in a slightly awkward way
senses.definition: happening at a moment that feels awkward or poorly timed
senses.definitionCN: 发生在让人觉得尴尬或不合适的时候
senses.example: An unexpected silence made the joke fall flat.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵突兀的沉默让那个笑话落了空。
senses.why: Surprise and discomfort are neighbours, so the word often carries a hint of awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶与不适本是邻居，因此这个词常常带着一点尴尬的意味。

senses.title: Costs that were not budgeted for
senses.definition: used of money that must be spent beyond what was planned
senses.definitionCN: 形容超出原计划必须支出的钱款
senses.example: Unexpected repairs ate up the whole holiday fund.
senses.exampleCN: 预算外的修理费吃掉了整笔度假基金。
senses.why: Whatever was not planned for will also not be budgeted for.
senses.whyCN: 凡是没被计划在内的，也就没被编进预算。

intro.en: Expect comes from Latin through French, and the negative adjective was formed in English.
intro.cn: expect 经由法语来自拉丁语，带否定前缀的形容词则是英语自己造出来的。

items.en: Exspectare meant to look out for, from ex-, out, and spectare, to look.
items.cn: exspectare 意为「向外张望」，由 ex-（向外）与 spectare（看）构成。

items.en: The verb passed into French as expecter, keeping the sense of awaiting.
items.cn: 这个动词进入法语作 expecter，保留「等候」之义。

items.en: English borrowed it as expect and used it for awaiting something with confidence.
items.cn: 英语借入作 expect，用来表示有把握地等候某事。

items.en: The sense widened to predicting or supposing what will happen.
items.cn: 其意义扩展为预测或设想将会发生的事。

items.en: Un- placed before the past participle gave a word for what nobody looked for.
items.cn: 在过去分词前加 un-，就得到了表示「没人张望过之事」的词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the expect family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 expect 词族，近义组汇集表示惊讶的词。

entries.definition: to think that something will happen
in a way nobody planned for
a belief that something will happen

entries.definitionCN: 未受影响的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: known in advance to be coming

normalIntro.en: The word is a looking-forward verb with the looking taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是「向前张望」的动词，把张望拿走了。

normal.en: Un- plus expected: not looked forward to.
normal.cn: un- 加 expected：没被张望过的。

normal.en: Expect comes from spectare, to look, which is also in spectator.
normal.cn: expect 源自 spectare（看），spectator 里也有这个词根。

normal.en: Unexpectedly is the adverb that usually sits next to arrive or happen.
normal.cn: unexpectedly 这个副词常跟在 arrive 或 happen 旁边。

normal.en: Completely unexpected is a very common intensifier pattern.
normal.cn: completely unexpected 是很常见的加强说法。

normal.en: Unexpected expenses and unexpected guests are two familiar collocations.
normal.cn: unexpected expenses 与 unexpected guests 是两个熟悉的搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a door swinging open to a room full of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象门一推开，屋里站满朋友。

abstract.en: See a test paper turned over with a question you never revised.
abstract.cn: 看一张翻过来的试卷，上面有一道从没复习的题。

abstract.en: Feel the half-second before the brain catches up with the eyes.
abstract.cn: 体会眼睛看到、脑子还没跟上之前的那半秒。

examples.en: Her arrival at the party was completely unexpected.
examples.cn: 她出现在聚会上，完全出乎大家的意料。

examples.en: An unexpected letter changed his plans for the year.
examples.cn: 一封意外的来信改变了他这一年的计划。

examples.en: Unexpectedly, the old machine started again on its own.
examples.cn: 出乎意料的是，那台旧机器又自己转了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺一看是个屁的」——推门一看根本不是那人，白等一场，真是意外。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ expected，expect 源自拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望），由 ex-（向外）+ spectare（看）构成

sensesIntro.en: One negation of looking ahead spreads to visitors, results, moments, and bills.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对「提前张望」的否定，蔓延到访客、结果、时刻与账单上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened to someone you did not know was coming.
core.cn: 核心意象：推开门看见一个你不知道会来的人。

branches.en: The core branch: what was not looked forward to at all.
branches.cn: 核心分支：完全没有被提前张望的事。

branches.en: The arrival branch: the person at the door.
branches.cn: 到来分支：门口站着的那个人。

branches.en: The result branch: an outcome nobody predicted.
branches.cn: 结果分支：没人预测到的结局。

branches.en: The timing branch: the moment that makes people wince.
branches.cn: 时机分支：让人尴尬的那个时刻。

branches.en: The money branch: the bill that was never planned.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：从未计划过的支出。

intro.en: The parts are an English prefix and a Latin-looking verb, all transparent in spelling.
intro.cn: 部件是英语前缀和一个带拉丁血统的动词，拼写上一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The looking root spectare also yields spectacle, spectator, and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「看」的词根 spectare 还生出 spectacle、spectator 与 inspect。

items.example: Spectare is the root of spectacle.
items.exampleCN: spectare 是 spectacle 的词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词后缀

items.example: An unforeseen delay cost them the train.
items.exampleCN: 一次未能预见的耽误让他们错过了火车。

definition_zh: 意外地；出乎意料地；没想到地；突然地
definition_en: in a way that nobody planned for or thought likely
core_image: 还没到门口，人就先一步出现了
scene: 本该下周到的包裹，第二天一早就放在了门口，她连睡衣都没换就笑了。The parcel arrived unexpectedly.
sceneCN: 这里 unexpectedly 是「意外地」（第 1 个义项：出乎意料）；句意为包裹意外地到了。人先于预期出现的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「意外的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「意外性」
词族核心动词，义为「期待；预料」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「如预料地」

senses.title: In a way that was not planned
senses.definition: in a way that nobody had planned for or believed likely
senses.definitionCN: 以没有人计划过、也不认为会发生的方式
senses.example: The meeting ended unexpectedly early and everyone went home by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议结束得出奇地早，中午大家就各自回家了。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the negative prefix of the adjective and simply says how the surprise happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了形容词的否定前缀，只是把「意外」这件事说成发生的方式。

senses.title: Without warning
senses.definition: used when something happens with no sign beforehand
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事发生前毫无迹象
senses.example: The lights went out unexpectedly in the middle of the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影放到一半，灯毫无预告地灭了。
senses.why: No expectation means no warning, so the adverb often means simply suddenly.
senses.whyCN: 没有预期也就没有预告，因此这个副词常常就相当于「突然」。

senses.title: Modifying a degree: surprisingly high or low
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say the degree is surprising
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明程度令人惊讶
senses.example: The new engine is unexpectedly quiet on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机在高速上出奇地安静。
senses.why: A degree that was not guessed can be attached to the verb like any other adverb of manner.
senses.whyCN: 没被猜到的程度，可以和别的方式副词一样挂在形容词前。

senses.title: Behaving in an unforeseen way
senses.definition: used of people who act in a manner others did not expect
senses.definitionCN: 形容人的举动与旁人的预期不符
senses.example: He reacted unexpectedly, laughing at news that should have hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反应出人意料，对着本该伤人的消息笑出声来。
senses.why: Behaviour that escapes prediction is judged from outside, which is exactly what an adverb marks.
senses.whyCN: 逃出预期的行为总由旁观者来评判，而副词正是这种评判的标记。

senses.title: Phrased to open a sentence
senses.definition: often placed at the start of a clause to comment on the whole news
senses.definitionCN: 常放在句首，对整句内容作评论
senses.example: Unexpectedly, the train left on time.
senses.exampleCN: 出乎意料的是，火车准点开走了。
senses.why: An adverb that judges an event can stand outside the clause and set the tone for it.
senses.whyCN: 一个评判事件的副词可以站到句子外面，为整句定调。

intro.en: The word is a chain of small parts: prefix, verb, participle ending, and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是一串小部件的接续：前缀、动词、分词词尾，再加副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Exspectare meant to look out for, from ex- and spectare, to look.
items.cn: exspectare 意为「向外张望」，由 ex- 与 spectare（看）构成。

items.en: French expecter carried the sense of waiting for something.
items.cn: 法语 expecter 带有「等候某事」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as expect and later used it for predicting.
items.cn: 英语借入动词作 expect，后来用以表示预测。

items.en: The adjective unexpectedly carries the negative prefix un- at its head.
items.cn: 形容词在词首带着否定前缀 un-。

items.en: -ly was added to the adjective, giving the adverb that marks how surprises happen.
items.cn: 形容词再加 -ly，得到标记意外发生的副词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the expect root, and the near-meaning group covers adverbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组收集 expect 词根的其他形式，近义组覆盖表示惊讶的副词。

entries.definition: the quality of being a surprise

entries.definitionCN: 毫无例外地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in a way that causes surprise
in a short and rough way

normalIntro.en: The adverb is a judgement placed next to a verb, so it tells you how the surprise arrived.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词是贴在动词旁的评判，告诉你意外是怎么发生的。

normal.en: Un- plus expectedly: not as foreseen.
normal.cn: un- 加 expectedly：不像被预见的那样。

normal.en: Arrive unexpectedly is the pattern learners meet most often.
normal.cn: arrive unexpectedly 是学习者最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: Before an adjective it marks surprising degree, as in unexpectedly high.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前时，它标记出人意料的程度，如 unexpectedly high。

normal.en: At the start of a clause it judges the whole sentence that follows.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，它评判后面整句话。

normal.en: The adjective is unexpected; the ending -ly adds manner.
normal.cn: 形容词是 unexpected，词尾 -ly 加上的正是「方式」。

abstract.en: Picture a doorbell ringing hours before you expect it.
abstract.cn: 想象门铃比预想的时间早了几个小时响起。

abstract.en: See a lift doors open on the wrong floor.
abstract.cn: 看电梯门在错的楼层打开。

abstract.en: Hear a voice say a name you had not spoken for years.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音说出你多年没叫过的名字。

examples.en: The old bridge collapsed unexpectedly on a dry, quiet night.
examples.cn: 那座旧桥在一个干燥安静的夜里意外坍塌。

examples.en: Unexpectedly, the shop had exactly the book she wanted.
examples.cn: 出乎意料的是，店里正好有她想要的那本书。

examples.en: Prices rose unexpectedly fast in the spring.
examples.cn: 春天物价出人意料地上涨得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺尼可斯派克替德利」——俺还没说请，人就替德利先到了，真是意外得很。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ expectedly，expect 源自拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望），词根 spectare 意为「看」

sensesIntro.en: One adverb of surprise works beside verbs, before adjectives, and at the head of a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示意外的副词，既能贴动词、又能修饰形容词，还能站到句首。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone arriving before they were expected.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没到预期就出现的人。

branches.en: The event branch: what happens without planning or warning.
branches.cn: 事件分支：没有计划也没有预告发生的事。

branches.en: The degree branch: a level nobody guessed.
branches.cn: 程度分支：没人猜到的程度。

branches.en: The behaviour branch: people acting against expectation.
branches.cn: 行为分支：举动违背预期的那些人。

branches.en: The comment branch: a word that opens the sentence and judges it.
branches.cn: 评注分支：放在句首评论整句的词。

branches.en: The plain event sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素的「意外事件」义。

intro.en: Four small pieces, all visible: un-, the verb expect, the participle ending, and -ly.
intro.cn: 四个小部件全都看得见：un-、动词 expect、分词词尾与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The looking root spectare also survives in spectator and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「看」的词根 spectare 也存在于 spectator 与 inspect 中。

definition_zh: 不公平的；不公正的；不合理的；不诚实（的竞争方式）
definition_en: not treating people equally or by the rules, and so unjust
core_image: 天平的一端被人悄悄按了下去
scene: 操场上分组，个子高的都被挑进一队，剩下的小个子只能拼成一队。The teams were obviously unfair.
sceneCN: 这里 unfair 是「不公平的」（第 1 个义项：对待不平等）；句意为分队明显不公平。被按下一端的天平正是这个词的核心意象。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不公正地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不公平；不公正」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「公平的；晴朗的」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「公平地；相当」

senses.title: Not treating people equally
senses.definition: not giving the same treatment, chance, or pay to everyone concerned
senses.definitionCN: 没有给相关的人同等的对待、机会或报酬
senses.example: It is unfair that only some students get the extra lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 只有部分学生能上补习课，这不公平。
senses.why: The prefix negates fair, a word for even-handed dealing, so unfair names whatever tilts the balance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 fair（不偏不倚的对待），于是 unfair 就是任何让天平倾斜的东西。

senses.title: Breaking the rules of a game or trade
senses.definition: used of an advantage gained by cheating or breaking agreed rules
senses.definitionCN: 形容靠作弊或违反约定规则取得的优势
senses.example: The referee punished him for unfair play.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因他不正当的比赛方式判了罚。
senses.why: Fair first meant pleasing and then pleasing according to the rules, so breaking them is unfair.
senses.whyCN: fair 先表示「令人满意」，再转为「合乎规则」，违反规则便是不公平。

senses.title: Not reasonable or justified
senses.definition: used of a demand, judgement, or comment that seems too harsh or too quick
senses.definitionCN: 形容要求、判断或评论过于苛刻或草率
senses.example: That is an unfair judgement on a first attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 对第一次尝试就下这样的判断并不合理。
senses.why: Fair also means reasonable, so whatever reason cannot justify is unfair.
senses.whyCN: fair 也有「合乎情理」之义，道理讲不通的自然就不合理。

senses.title: Hard on one particular person
senses.definition: used when something demands more of one person than the situation warrants
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事对某人的要求超出情势所该有的
senses.example: It was unfair on her to leave the whole mess at her door.
senses.exampleCN: 把这一团糟全推到她头上，对她太不公平。
senses.why: Complaints about balance are usually aimed at a named person who was made to carry more.
senses.whyCN: 关于失衡的抱怨往往落在一个被要求承担更多的人身上。

senses.title: Unjust in a legal or working sense
senses.titleCN: 不公正的（法律、劳动层面）
senses.definition: used in law and employment of decisions or treatment that violate justice
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与职场语境中，形容违反公正的决定或对待
senses.example: The court found the dismissal unfair and ordered compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这次解雇不公正，判令予以赔偿。
senses.why: The everyday sense of a tilted balance becomes a formal standard that courts can apply.
senses.whyCN: 日常语中「天平倾斜」的感受，变成法院可以引用的正式标准。

intro.en: Fair is an Old English word, and the negative form with un- appears much later.
intro.cn: fair 是古英语词，带 un- 的否定形式出现得晚得多。

items.en: Fæger meant beautiful or pleasant to look at.
items.cn: fæger 意为「美的、悦目的」。

items.en: The sense moved to free from blemish, then to just and even-handed.
items.cn: 其义由「无瑕」转向「公正、不偏」。

items.en: Unfair is built by prefixing un- to fair and is recorded from the Old English period in law.
items.cn: unfair 由 un- 加 fair 构成，早期法律文书中已有使用。

items.en: The sense expands to sport, trade, and schooling.
items.cn: 其意义扩展到体育、商业与学校。

items.en: Modern law uses unfair in fixed phrases about dismissal and competition.
items.cn: 现代法律在解雇与竞争等固定说法中沿用这个词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fair family, and the near-meaning group gathers words about injustice.
note.cn: 形近组是 fair 词族，近义组汇集表示不公的词。

entries.definitionCN: 不熟悉的（只是前缀相同，词根不同）

normalIntro.en: One prefix over a very old English word for beautiful and even.
normalIntro.cn: 一个前缀压在一个古英语老词上，那词本义是美与均匀。

normal.en: Un- plus fair: not even, not just.
normal.cn: un- 加 fair：不均，不公。

normal.en: It is unfair to plus a verb is the most common frame.
normal.cn: It is unfair to 加动词是最常见的句型。

normal.en: Unfair dismissal and unfair competition are fixed legal phrases.
normal.cn: unfair dismissal 与 unfair competition 是固定的法律用语。

normal.en: Fair also means pale or lovely weather, a reminder of its old sense of beauty.
normal.cn: fair 还表示「皮肤白」或「天气好」，提醒着它旧日的「美」义。

normal.en: Unfairness is the noun, unfairly the adverb of manner.
normal.cn: unfairness 是名词，unfairly 是方式副词。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with a thumb pressed on one pan.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆天平，一端被人用拇指按着。

abstract.en: See two children of different height told to reach the same shelf.
abstract.cn: 看两个高矮不同的孩子被要求够同一个架子。

abstract.en: Hear a whistle blown for a rule only one side must follow.
abstract.cn: 听一声哨响，只对一方生效的规则。

examples.en: It is unfair to blame the youngest for the whole accident.
examples.cn: 把整个事故都怪到最小的孩子头上不公平。

examples.en: The company was fined for unfair competition.
examples.cn: 这家公司因不公平竞争被罚款。

examples.en: She was treated unfairly and said so openly.
examples.cn: 她受到了不公正的对待，并公开说了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺费耳」——同样是排队，俺费了耳朵听了一下午，却被人插队，太不公平。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ fair，fair 来自古英语 fæger（美的、悦目的），中世纪转义为「公正、不偏」

sensesIntro.en: A tilted scale covers unequal treatment, broken rules, harsh judgement, and unjust law.
sensesIntro.cn: 一杆倾斜的天平，覆盖不平等的对待、违规、苛刻的评判与不公的法律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with a hand pressing one pan down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手下压着一端的天平。

branches.en: The everyday branch: different chances for different people.
branches.cn: 日常分支：不同的人得到不同的机会。

branches.en: The rules branch: a game or market where cheating pays.
branches.cn: 规则分支：作弊能得利的比赛或市场。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a verdict too quick to be just.
branches.cn: 判断分支：草率下定的结论。

branches.en: The personal branch: one person asked to carry too much.
branches.cn: 个人分支：被要求承担过多的人。

branches.en: The legal branch: fixed phrases for courts and contracts.
branches.cn: 法律分支：法院与合同中的固定说法。

intro.en: The word is a negative prefix on a native English adjective, so the parts explain themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本土形容词加否定前缀，部件本身就能说明意思。

latinIntro.en: Fair is not Latin, so the Latin section lists only its remote Germanic ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: fair 不是拉丁语词，拉丁部分只列出它更远的日耳曼语祖先。

items.exampleCN: 一条不公正的法律被废除了。

items.example: A biased report is unfair to readers.
items.exampleCN: 偏袒的报道对读者不公。

definition_zh: 不公平地；不公正地；不正当地
definition_en: in a way that gives people unequal or unjust treatment
core_image: 分苹果时，最大的那个总被递给同一个人
scene: 分奖金那天，干活最多的人拿得最少，大家低头不语。He was treated unfairly.
sceneCN: 这里 unfairly 是「不公正地」（第 1 个义项：对待不公）；句意为他受到了不公正的对待。最大的果子总递给同一个人，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不公平的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不公平」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「公平地；相当」
近义词，由 unjust 加 -ly 构成，义为「不公正地」

senses.title: In a way that gives unequal shares
senses.definition: in a way that gives some people less than they deserve
senses.definitionCN: 以让某些人所得少于应得的方式
senses.example: The prize money was unfairly divided among the players.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金在队员之间分得不公平。
senses.why: The adverb adds a manner to fair, and the negative prefix turns that manner into an unequal one.
senses.whyCN: 副词把「方式」加到 fair 上，否定前缀又把这种方变成了不平等的方式。

senses.title: By wronging a person
senses.definition: used with verbs such as blame, accuse, or punish to say the target was wronged
senses.definitionCN: 与 blame、accuse、punish 等动词连用，说明被对待者受了冤屈
senses.example: She was unfairly blamed for a mistake made by the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 整队犯的错却被不公正地算在她头上。
senses.why: Balance is broken by pushing the weight onto one person, which is exactly what the adverb describes.
senses.whyCN: 把重量全压到一个人身上就是失衡，这正是这个副词所描写的。

senses.title: Against the rules of a contest
senses.definition: in a manner that breaks agreed rules or takes a hidden advantage
senses.definitionCN: 以违背约定规则或暗中占便宜的方式
senses.example: One firm competed unfairly by copying a rival design.
senses.exampleCN: 一家公司抄袭对手的设计进行不正当竞争。
senses.why: Fair play is a game played by rule, so playing off-rule is doing it unfairly.
senses.whyCN: fair play 是按规则进行的比赛，不照规则出牌就是不公正。

senses.title: In employment or law
senses.definition: used in legal and workplace statements about treatment that cannot be justified
senses.definitionCN: 用于法律与职场陈述，指无法说明理由的对待
senses.example: The tribunal ruled that he had been dismissed unfairly.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭裁定他遭到了不公正的解雇。
senses.why: Legal language takes the everyday sense of a tilt and makes it a ground for a claim.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把日常语中天平倾斜的感觉，变成了提出诉讼的理由。

senses.title: In a degree that seems excessive
senses.definition: used before a criticism to suggest the judgement goes too far
senses.definitionCN: 放在批评之前，暗示这个评判过头了
senses.example: It would be unfairly harsh to reject every draft.
senses.exampleCN: 把每一稿都否掉未免过分严厉。
senses.why: What is too harsh is not balanced, and the adverb carries that feeling of excess.
senses.whyCN: 过严即失衡，这个副词把那种过头的感觉带了出来。

intro.en: The adverb is built in English from fair, the negative prefix un-, and the ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个副词是英语自己拼起来的：fair 加否定前缀 un- 和词尾 -ly。

items.en: Fæger described something beautiful or pleasing.
items.cn: fæger 形容美丽、悦目之物。

items.en: Fair came to mean just and even-handed in judgement.
items.cn: fair 转为表示「公正、判断不偏」。

items.en: Un- was added in Middle English law, giving unfair for unjust dealings.
items.cn: 中古英语法律文中已加 un-，形成 unfair 指不公正的做法。

items.en: -ly turned the adjective into an adverb of manner in ordinary use.
items.cn: 在普通用法中，-ly 把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Unfairly now clusters with blame, accuse, and dismiss in legal and news texts.
items.cn: 如今在法律与新闻文本中，这个词常与 blame、accuse、dismiss 搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fair family, and the near-meaning group covers adverbs of injustice.
note.cn: 形近组收集 fair 词族，近义组覆盖表示不公的副词。

entries.definition: equally, or to a moderate degree

entries.definitionCN: 总是；可靠地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in a way that is not morally right
in an equal and just way

normalIntro.en: The adverb is the adjective plus a manner ending, nothing more.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是形容词加一个方式词尾，再无别的。

normal.en: Unfairly is unfair plus -ly, the regular English adverb pattern.
normal.cn: unfairly 就是 unfair 加 -ly，英语规则的副词构词方式。

normal.en: Treated unfairly is the passive frame learners hear most.
normal.cn: treated unfairly 是学习者最常听到的被动搭配。

normal.en: Unfairly dismissed is a fixed phrase in employment law.
normal.cn: unfairly dismissed 是雇佣法中的固定说法。

normal.en: Unfairly blamed and unfairly accused both suggest a victim.
normal.cn: unfairly blamed 与 unfairly accused 都暗示有人受了冤。

normal.en: Fairly is the opposite in manner; fair is the opposite in quality.
normal.cn: 副词的反义是 fairly，形容词的反义是 fair。

abstract.en: Picture one child always getting the sliced-off, smaller half.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子每次都拿到切下去的、小的那一半。

abstract.en: See a referee turn his head at the foul.
abstract.cn: 看裁判在犯规那一刻把头转开。

abstract.en: Hear a verdict read out that the crowd meets with silence.
abstract.cn: 听宣判念出，人群以沉默回应。

examples.en: The two workers were unfairly paid for the same job.
examples.cn: 两个工人做同样的活，报酬却不公平。

examples.en: He felt he had been unfairly accused.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己被冤枉了。

examples.en: She argued that the contract had been unfairly drawn up.
examples.cn: 她辩称这份合同拟得不公正。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺费耳历」——俺费了耳力听完，结果还是被人占了便宜，太不公平。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ fair + 副词后缀 -ly，fair 来自古英语 fæger（美的、悦目的）

sensesIntro.en: One manner, tilted, appears in shares, accusations, contests, and court rulings.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种倾斜的方式，出现在分配、指责、比赛与判决里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the best apple handed to the same person every time.
core.cn: 核心意象：最好的苹果每次都递给同一个人。

branches.en: The shares branch: less than someone deserved.
branches.cn: 分配分支：所得少于应得。

branches.en: The accusation branch: weight pushed onto one person.
branches.cn: 指责分支：重量被压到一个人身上。

branches.en: The contest branch: rules bent for advantage.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：为占便宜而弯折规则。

branches.en: The legal branch: treatment that cannot be justified.
branches.cn: 法律分支：无法说明理由的对待。

branches.en: The manner branch: a judgement that goes too far.
branches.cn: 方式分支：过头的评判。

intro.en: Three parts, all ordinary English: prefix, adjective, adverb ending.
intro.cn: 三个部件都是常见英语：前缀、形容词、副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin layer here; fair is a native word, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这一层没有拉丁语，fair 是本土词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 一道不公的命令被拒绝。
不平等的报酬就是不公。

definition_zh: 不幸的；倒霉的；可惜的；令人遗憾的；不恰当的
definition_en: having bad luck, or being a regrettable thing to say or do
core_image: 刚出门就下雨，而伞恰好留在了家里
scene: 他赶到车站时，车门正好在眼前合上，下一班要等一小时。It was an unfortunate start to the day.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunate 是「倒霉的、不幸的」（第 1 个义项：运气不好）；句意为这一天的开头很不顺。刚出门就下雨而伞留在家里，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不幸地；遗憾的是」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「幸运的」
词族核心名词，义为「运气；财富」
用 mis- 表坏的近义词，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: Having bad luck
senses.definition: suffering from bad luck or a bad turn of events
senses.definitionCN: 遭遇坏运气或事态的不利转折
senses.example: The unfortunate passengers spent the night in the station.
senses.exampleCN: 那些倒霉的乘客在车站里过了一夜。
senses.why: The prefix negates fortune, which came from Latin fors, chance, so unfortunate means without good chance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 fortune（源自拉丁语 fors，机遇），unfortunate 就是没有好机缘。

senses.title: Regrettable rather than tragic
senses.definition: used of something mildly bad that one wishes had not happened
senses.definitionCN: 形容某件不太好、但愿没有发生的事
senses.example: It is unfortunate that the meeting falls on a public holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 会议恰逢公共假日，真是可惜。
senses.why: Bad luck on a small scale is simply a pity, so the word softens into regret.
senses.whyCN: 小尺度的坏运气就只是「可惜」，于是这个词软化成遗憾。

senses.title: Said of a person who deserves sympathy
senses.definition: used to describe someone who has been badly treated or badly served
senses.definitionCN: 形容受到苛待或委屈而值得同情的人
senses.example: He was unfortunate enough to be standing nearest the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他倒霉到刚好站在门边。
senses.why: Chance picks its victims without reason, and the word marks whoever chance picked.
senses.whyCN: 机遇挑人从不讲理由，这个词就标记出被挑中的那一个。

senses.title: Words or actions in poor taste
senses.definition: used of a remark or choice that is awkward and causes offence by accident
senses.definitionCN: 形容某句话或某个选择不巧令人不快，并非有意
senses.example: An unfortunate remark ruined the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不恰当的玩笑毁掉了那番祝酒。
senses.why: A choice that brings bad consequences feels like bad luck even when it was your own.
senses.whyCN: 一个带来坏后果的选择，即使出于自己，也像坏运气一般。

senses.title: A combination of events that go wrong together
senses.definition: used of a coincidence or set of conditions that produce a bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容若干条件凑在一起造成坏结果的巧合
senses.example: An unfortunate combination of wind and rain delayed the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风雨不幸地凑在一起，让航班延误了。
senses.why: When several chances line up badly, the whole arrangement carries the label.
senses.whyCN: 当几个偶然凑得极糟，整个组合都带上了这个标签。

intro.en: Fortune comes from Latin through French, and English made the negative adjective with un-.
intro.cn: fortune 经由法语来自拉丁语，英语自己用 un- 造出否定形容词。

items.en: Fortuna was the goddess of chance, from fors, meaning luck or accident.
items.cn: Fortuna 是掌管机运的女神，出自 fors，意为「运气、偶然」。

items.en: Fortune entered French as a word for chance and what chance brings.
items.cn: fortune 进入法语，指机遇以及机遇带来的东西。

items.en: English borrowed fortune, which also came to mean wealth.
items.cn: 英语借入 fortune，后来又引申为财富。

items.en: Fortunate was formed from fortune, and un- was prefixed to it.
items.cn: fortunate 由 fortune 派生，再被加上前缀 un-。

items.en: The adjective softens into pity and mild regret in modern usage.
items.cn: 现代用法中，这个形容词软化为同情与轻微的遗憾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fortune family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of bad luck.
note.cn: 形近组是 fortune 词族，近义组汇集表示不幸的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is fortune with a negative prefix, so it means chance turned against you.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带了否定前缀的 fortune，意思是机遇没有站在你这边。

normal.en: Un- plus fortunate: without good fortune.
normal.cn: un- 加 fortunate：没有好运。

normal.en: It is unfortunate that is the polite frame for bad news.
normal.cn: It is unfortunate that 是通报坏消息时客气的说法。

normal.en: An unfortunate remark points to awkward timing far more than to evil intent.
normal.cn: an unfortunate remark 更多指向时机不巧，而非恶意。

normal.en: Unfortunately is the sentence opener; unfortunate is the description.
normal.cn: unfortunately 常作句首语，unfortunate 用来描述人或事。

normal.en: Fortune also means wealth, from the same idea of chance.
normal.cn: fortune 还表示财富，同出「机遇」这一观念。

abstract.en: Picture a bus doors closing as the runner reaches the stop.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者刚跑到站台，车门正好合上。

abstract.en: See a picnic blanket spread under a sky just breaking.
abstract.cn: 看野餐布铺开，天色却正要变坏。

abstract.en: Hear a joke land one word too late.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话只差一个词就落空。

examples.en: The unfortunate family lost both their home and their car.
examples.cn: 这个不幸的家庭同时失去了房子和车子。

examples.en: It is unfortunate that no one told her earlier.
examples.cn: 遗憾的是没有人早点告诉她。

examples.en: An unfortunate choice of words turned a small dispute into a fight.
examples.cn: 一句不恰当的措辞把小小的争执变成了吵架。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺勿车呢特」——俺赶车总搭不上车，误了这趟又误那趟，真倒霉。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ fortunate，fortune 源自拉丁语 fors（机遇）与 Fortuna（机运女神），经法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: Chance, removed of its good side, runs from real hardship to a small awkward remark.
sensesIntro.cn: 把机缘好的一面去掉，从真正的困厄一直延伸到一句不巧的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an umbrella left at home just as the rain begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚下雨时，伞恰好留在家里。

branches.en: The luck branch: a person chance treated badly.
branches.cn: 运气分支：被机遇薄待的人。

branches.en: The pity branch: a small bad thing worth a sigh.
branches.cn: 惋惜分支：值得叹一口气的小坏事。

branches.en: The manners branch: words that sound wrong in the room.
branches.cn: 礼仪分支：在那个场合显得不妥的话。

branches.en: The coincidence branch: several conditions meeting badly.
branches.cn: 巧合分支：几个条件凑得极糟。

branches.en: The plain sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素义项。

intro.en: An English prefix sits on a noun that came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: 一个英语前缀压在一个经法语来自拉丁语的名词上。

latinIntro.en: The root of chance, fors, sits under Fortuna and gives the family its oldest layer.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「机遇」的词根 fors 藏在 Fortuna 之下，是这一族最古老的一层。

items.example: An unlucky toss lost the match.
items.exampleCN: 一次倒霉的掷币让他们输掉了比赛。

items.example: A regrettable error was corrected quietly.
items.exampleCN: 一个令人遗憾的错误被悄悄纠正了。

definition_zh: 不幸地；遗憾的是；不巧；可惜
definition_en: in a way that is bad luck or a cause of regret, often used to open a sentence
core_image: 话还没说完，先一声轻轻的叹气
scene: 电话那头安静了一会儿，然后才传来婉拒的答复。Unfortunately, the tickets were already gone.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunately 是「遗憾的是」（第 2 个义项：表示惋惜的评注）；句意为可惜票已经卖完了。一声先于说话的叹气，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不幸的」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「幸运地」
词族核心名词，义为「运气；财富」
用 mis- 表坏的近义词，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: By bad luck
senses.definition: by an unlucky turn of events rather than by anyone fault
senses.definitionCN: 由于事态的不巧转折，而非任何人的过错
senses.example: Unfortunately, the rain started just as the ceremony began.
senses.exampleCN: 不巧的是，仪式刚开始就下起了雨。
senses.why: The adverb returns to the oldest sense of fortune as chance and says the chance went wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词回到 fortune 最古老的「机遇」之义，只是说机遇走坏了。

senses.title: Regrettably, used as a comment
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to soften bad or unwelcome news
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用来软化坏消息或不那么受欢迎的答复
senses.example: Unfortunately, we cannot offer you the position.
senses.exampleCN: 很遗憾，这个职位我们无法录用你。
senses.why: A word of bad chance placed outside the sentence turns into a polite frame for news.
senses.whyCN: 被放到句子外面的「坏运气」，就成了一种通报消息的礼貌包装。

senses.title: At a badly chosen moment
senses.definition: used of something that happens at an awkward time
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事发生在很尴尬的时间点
senses.example: The announcement came unfortunately close to the election.
senses.exampleCN: 这项宣布来得离选举太近，很不凑巧。
senses.why: Timing is part of chance, so a bad hour is a small piece of bad fortune.
senses.whyCN: 时机本是机遇的一部分，因此一个坏时刻就是一小片坏运气。

senses.title: With real loss or hardship
senses.definition: used when the outcome involves genuine harm to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于结果确实对某人造成伤害的场合
senses.example: Unfortunately, the files had not been saved.
senses.exampleCN: 不幸的是，那些文件没有保存。
senses.why: The mild and the grave uses sit on one scale, and only the context sets the weight.
senses.whyCN: 轻重两种用法在同一条刻度上，只有语境才决定它的分量。

senses.title: In a reply, as a soft no
senses.definition: used in conversation as a gentle way of refusing or correcting
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中委婉地拒绝或纠正他人
senses.example: Unfortunately not, the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉不行，那家店六点就关门了。
senses.why: Polite refusals borrow the language of chance so that nobody takes the blame.
senses.whyCN: 委婉的拒绝借用了「运气」的说法，好让谁都不必担责。

intro.en: The adverb is unfortunate plus -ly, with fortune reaching English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 unfortunate 加 -ly，而 fortune 经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Fors meant chance, and Fortuna personified it.
items.cn: fors 意为机遇，Fortuna 则是它的拟人化。

items.en: Fortune named chance and what chance gave, good or bad.
items.cn: fortune 指机遇以及它给予的东西，好坏皆可。

items.en: English adopted fortune, later extending it to wealth.
items.cn: 英语采用 fortune，后来延伸到财富。

items.en: Fortunate and unfortunate were built from the noun in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪由这个名词构成 fortunate 与 unfortunate。

items.en: -ly produced the adverb, which settled at the head of sentences.
items.cn: 加 -ly 得到副词，后来固定在句首使用。

note.en: The look-alike group holds fortune forms, and the near-meaning group gathers sentence adverbs of regret.
note.cn: 形近组是 fortune 的各种形式，近义组汇集表示遗憾的句子副词。

entries.definition: in a way that deserves regret

normalIntro.en: A sentence-opening adverb built from the noun fortune with two small additions.
normalIntro.cn: 一个放在句首的副词，由名词 fortune 加两个小部件而成。

normal.en: Un- plus fortunately: by bad luck.
normal.cn: un- 加 fortunately：运气不好。

normal.en: It almost always comes first in its clause, followed by a comma.
normal.cn: 它几乎总在小句开头，后面加一个逗号。

normal.en: Unfortunately not is a common soft refusal in speech.
normal.cn: unfortunately not 是口语中常见的委婉拒绝。

normal.en: Fortunately is the buoyant twin used for good outcomes.
normal.cn: fortunately 是它的乐观孪生词，用于好结果。

normal.en: Unfortunately for someone narrows the bad luck to one person.
normal.cn: unfortunately for someone 把坏运气缩到某一个人身上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised half way before the refusal is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象拒绝还没说出口，一只手先半举起来。

abstract.en: Hear the sigh that comes before the word on the phone.
abstract.cn: 听电话里那个词之前的一声叹气。

abstract.en: See a weather app open with rain on every day of the trip.
abstract.cn: 看旅行那几天天气预报上全是雨。

examples.en: Unfortunately, the last train had already left when we arrived.
examples.cn: 可惜的是，我们到的时候末班车已经开走了。

examples.en: Unfortunately for him, the only seat was in the sun.
examples.cn: 对他来说不幸的是，唯一的座位在太阳底下。

examples.en: She answered, unfortunately, that the file was lost.
examples.cn: 她遗憾地回答，那份档案丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺勿车呢特利」——俺赶车总搭不上，一趟趟都误了，说起来只能叹口气。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ fortunate + 副词后缀 -ly，fortune 源自拉丁语 fors（机遇），经法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One comment of bad chance covers real loss, awkward timing, and a soft no in conversation.
sensesIntro.cn: 一句「运气不好」的评注，覆盖真实损失、不巧的时机与对话中的委婉拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sigh that comes before the bad news.
core.cn: 核心意象：坏消息之前那一声轻轻的叹气。

branches.en: The luck branch: from a drizzle to a lost file.
branches.cn: 运气分支：从一阵小雨到丢失的文件。

branches.en: The comment branch: the word that opens the sentence.
branches.cn: 评注分支：放在句首的那个词。

branches.en: The timing branch: the wrong hour for an announcement.
branches.cn: 时机分支：宣布所用的错误时刻。

branches.en: The conversational branch: a gentle way to say no.
branches.cn: 会话分支：温和地说「不」。

branches.en: The frame that repeats in every regret.
branches.cn: 每一份遗憾都重复使用的那个框架。

intro.en: The adverb is a prefix, a Latin-derived noun, an adjective ending, and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个副词由一个前缀、一个来自拉丁的名词、一个形容词词尾与 -ly 组成。

latinIntro.en: Fors and Fortuna give the family its Latin base.
latinIntro.cn: fors 与 Fortuna 提供了这一族的拉丁基础。

items.meaning: in a way that deserves regret

definition_zh: 不友好的；冷淡的；不友善的；不利的
definition_en: not kind or welcoming to others, or not helpful to something
core_image: 门口挂着牌子，人一走近就把窗帘拉上
scene: 新搬来的邻居遇到楼道里迎面走来的人，笑着点头，对方却目不斜视地走过去。The neighbours were polite but unfriendly.
sceneCN: 这里 unfriendly 是「冷淡的、不友好的」（第 1 个义项：对人缺乏善意）；句意为邻居们客气但冷淡。人一靠近就拉上窗帘，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不友好；冷淡」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「友好的」
词族核心名词，义为「朋友」
肯定形式加 -ness 的名词，义为「友善」

senses.title: Cold in manner towards others
senses.definition: behaving in a cold or unwelcoming way towards other people
senses.definitionCN: 以冷淡、不欢迎的方式对待他人
senses.example: The shop assistant was unfriendly but not rude.
senses.exampleCN: 那个店员不友好，却还没到粗鲁的地步。
senses.why: The prefix turns friendly inside out, so the quality of a friend is exactly what is missing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀把 friendly（像朋友一样的）翻了个面，缺的正是朋友那份情谊。

senses.title: A place or group that gives no warmth
senses.definition: used of a place, crowd, or atmosphere that makes people feel unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个场所、人群或气氛让人觉得自己不受欢迎
senses.example: The club had an unfriendly feel, all dark wood and low voices.
senses.exampleCN: 那个俱乐部气氛冷淡，全是深色木饰和低低的说话声。
senses.why: A room takes its mood from the people in it, so a cold crowd makes a cold place.
senses.whyCN: 屋子从人身上取得气氛，人冷淡，地方也就冷。

senses.title: Harsh or hostile in a look or tone
senses.definition: used of a gaze, tone, or remark that shows dislike
senses.definitionCN: 形容流露出反感的眼神、语气或话语
senses.example: He gave the newcomer an unfriendly stare.
senses.exampleCN: 他不友善地盯着新来的人。
senses.why: Whatever warmth would lie in a greeting is reversed, and the face closes.
senses.whyCN: 本该在问候里的那份暖意被反转，脸上就关起了门。

senses.title: Working against something
senses.titleCN: 不利的；不友好的（技术、环境语境）
senses.definition: used of systems, designs, or policies that are hard on users or the environment
senses.definitionCN: 形容对使用者或环境不友善的系统、设计或政策
senses.example: Critics called the new form user-unfriendly and needlessly long.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说新表格对使用者不友好，而且长得没有必要。
senses.why: The everyday sense of not being kind moves easily onto things that treat people badly.
senses.whyCN: 日常语中「不厚道」的意思，很容易挪到苛待人的事物上。

senses.title: Not favourable to a cause
senses.definition: used of conditions or attitudes that oppose a plan or interest
senses.definitionCN: 形容不利于某项计划或利益的条件与态度
senses.example: The town proved unfriendly to new businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 事实证明，这个镇子对新企业并不友好。
senses.why: Anything that receives you coldly makes your work harder, so unfriendly also means unfavourable.
senses.whyCN: 任何冷脸相迎的东西都会让你的工作更难，于是「不友好」也等于「不利」。

intro.en: Friendly is an English adjective on the old Germanic noun friend, with the negative prefix added.
intro.cn: friendly 是古日耳曼语名词 friend 派生的英语形容词，否定前缀是后加的。

items.en: Freond meant a friend, from a Germanic root meaning to love.
items.cn: freond 意为「朋友」，词根在日耳曼语中表示「爱」。

items.en: The noun carried duties as well as affection, as in a friend in need.
items.cn: 这个名词除情谊外还带着义务，如患难中的朋友。

items.en: Freendly appeared as an adjective describing kind behaviour.
items.cn: freendly 作为形容词出现，描写厚道的举止。

items.en: Un- was added to describe the opposite temper, often of looks and places.
items.cn: 加 un- 表示相反的性格，常用于神情与场所。

items.en: Modern compounds extend it to designs and policies, as in user-unfriendly.
items.cn: 现代的复合词又把它扩展到设计与政策，如 user-unfriendly。

note.en: The look-alike group is the friend family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for coldness.
note.cn: 形近组是 friend 词族，近义组汇集表示冷淡的词。

entries.definition: a person you know well and like

entries.definitionCN: 总是（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word is friend turned into an adjective and then turned against itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 friend 先变成形容词，又被反过来用。

normal.en: Un- plus friendly: without the warmth of a friend.
normal.cn: un- 加 friendly：没有朋友的那份暖意。

normal.en: Be unfriendly to someone is the usual preposition.
normal.cn: be unfriendly to someone 是常见的介词搭配。

normal.en: User-unfriendly shows how a manner word moves onto objects.
normal.cn: user-unfriendly 显示了方式类形容词如何移到器物上。

normal.en: The ending -ly here makes an adjective, as in lovely and costly.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ly 构成形容词，与 lovely、costly 同理。

normal.en: Unfriendliness is the noun, though most people use coldness instead.
normal.cn: 名词是 unfriendliness，不过多数人更常说 coldness。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain drawn the moment footsteps reach the door.
abstract.cn: 想象脚步声刚到门口，窗帘就被拉上。

abstract.en: See a nod that stops half way.
abstract.cn: 看一个点到一半就收住的头。

abstract.en: Hear a greeting answered with a single flat syllable.
abstract.cn: 听一声问候只换回一个平板的音节。

examples.en: The staff were not rude, just unfriendly.
examples.cn: 店员并不粗鲁，只是冷淡。

examples.en: An unfriendly silence greeted his joke.
examples.cn: 他的笑话只换来一片冷淡的沉默。

examples.en: The tax rules are unfriendly to small firms.
examples.cn: 这些税收规则对小公司不利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺勿弗伦德利」——俺没把人家当朋友待，人家自然也不给好脸。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ friendly，friendly 由古英语 freond（朋友）派生，词根在日耳曼语中表示「爱」

sensesIntro.en: One missing warmth spreads from faces to rooms, to the look in an eye, and to rules and forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份缺席的暖意，从脸上蔓延到屋子、眼神，再到规则与表格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain pulled shut as someone walks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人走近时被拉上的窗帘。

branches.en: The personal branch: the person who does not meet your eyes.
branches.cn: 个人分支：不与你对视的那个人。

branches.en: The place branch: a room that feels shut.
branches.cn: 场所分支：让人感到关起来的房间。

branches.en: The expression branch: the stare and the flat tone.
branches.cn: 神情分支：那道目光与平板的语气。

branches.en: The technical branch: forms and conditions that work against you.
branches.cn: 技术分支：与你作对的表格与条件。

branches.en: The plain everyday sense most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素的日常义。

intro.en: A native English noun, an adjective ending, and a negative prefix make up the word.
intro.cn: 本土英语名词、形容词词尾与否定前缀共同构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer; friend is Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语层，friend 属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: a person you love and trust

items.exampleCN: 新应用对使用者不友好。
一群带有敌意的人聚集在外面。

definition_zh: 不快乐的；不幸福的；不满意的；不幸的
definition_en: sad, dissatisfied, or not well suited to a situation
core_image: 生日蛋糕前的蜡烛烧了半天，脸上却提不起笑
scene: 搬进新家的第一个晚上，孩子在陌生的床上翻来覆去，说想回去。She was unhappy in the new town.
sceneCN: 这里 unhappy 是「不快乐的」（第 1 个义项：心情不悦）；句意为她在那座新城里过得不开心。烛光里提不起笑的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不快乐地；不幸地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不快乐；不幸」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「快乐的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「幸福」

senses.title: Sad in mood
senses.definition: feeling sad or low over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里感到难过、情绪低落
senses.example: He was unhappy for weeks after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家后的几个星期他一直不高兴。
senses.why: The prefix denies happy, and happy itself came from hap, meaning chance or good luck.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 happy，而 happy 本出自 hap（机遇、好运），于是不快乐就是没有好运相伴。

senses.title: Not satisfied with something
senses.definition: displeased with a decision, a service, or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某个决定、服务或状况感到不满
senses.example: Many parents were unhappy about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家长对新课表不满。
senses.why: To be without good luck is to be without what you wanted, which reads as complaint.
senses.whyCN: 没有好运也就没有所求之物，这份欠缺读起来就是不满。

senses.title: A period or relationship without joy
senses.definition: used of times or relationships that contain more sorrow than joy
senses.definitionCN: 形容包含更多悲伤而少有欢乐的时期或关系
senses.example: It was an unhappy marriage from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 那段婚姻从一开始就不幸福。
senses.why: A stretch of life inherits the feeling of the people living it.
senses.whyCN: 一段时光会继承生活在其中的人的感受。

senses.title: Unlucky in its timing or outcome
senses.definition: used of an event that turns out badly or comes at a bad moment
senses.definitionCN: 形容结果不好或发生得不巧的事
senses.example: It was an unhappy coincidence that both letters arrived the same day.
senses.exampleCN: 两封信同一天到，真是不巧的巧合。
senses.why: The old sense of hap as chance explains why unhappy can still mean unlucky.
senses.whyCN: hap 原本就是「机遇」，这解释了为什么 unhappy 至今还能表示「不巧」。

senses.title: Not appropriate or happy in choice
senses.definition: used of a word or choice that is unfortunate rather than wrong
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个词或选择不恰当，而不是错误
senses.example: An unhappy phrase made the report sound cold.
senses.exampleCN: 一个失当的措辞让报告听起来冷冰冰。
senses.why: Happy once meant fitting or apt, so an unhappy phrase is one that does not fit.
senses.whyCN: happy 曾经也有「恰当、合宜」之义，因此 unhappy phrase 指不合适的说法。

intro.en: Happy comes from the old noun hap, chance, and the negative prefix was added in English.
intro.cn: happy 来自古词 hap（机遇），否定前缀是英语自己加上去的。

items.en: Happ meant chance or luck, and English took the noun early.
items.cn: happ 意为机遇、运气，英语很早就借入了这个名词。

items.en: Happy first meant lucky or favoured by chance.
items.cn: happy 最初意为「幸运的、得其时运」。

items.en: The sense shifted from good luck to good feeling.
items.cn: 其义由「好运」转向「好心情」。

items.en: Unhappy is recorded from the seventeenth century for sadness and displeasure.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，unhappy 有悲伤与不满的用法记录。

items.en: The older sense of unlucky survives in phrases about coincidences.
items.cn: 较古的「不巧」之义仍存于讲巧合的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the happy family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for sadness.
note.cn: 形近组是 happy 词族，近义组汇集表示悲伤的词。

entries.definitionCN: 不便使用的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word denies an old word for luck, which is why sadness and bad timing share one form.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定了古老的「运气」一词，所以悲伤与不巧共用同一形态。

normal.en: Un- plus happy: not favoured by luck.
normal.cn: un- 加 happy：没被运气眷顾。

normal.en: Be unhappy about is the usual pattern for complaints.
normal.cn: be unhappy about 是表达不满的常见搭配。

normal.en: Perhaps and happen come from the same hap root.
normal.cn: perhaps 与 happen 同出 hap 这个词根。

normal.en: Unhappier and unhappiest change the y to i before the endings.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级要把 y 变成 i 再加词尾。

normal.en: Unhappiness is the noun, and it is uncountable.
normal.cn: unhappiness 是名词，且不可数。

abstract.en: Picture a child sitting on an unmade bed in a new room.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子坐在新房间里没铺好的床上。

abstract.en: See candles burning down over an untouched cake.
abstract.cn: 看蜡烛烧下去，蛋糕却没人动。

abstract.en: Hear a laugh that stops a moment too early.
abstract.cn: 听一声笑得早了半拍就停下的笑。

examples.en: The children were unhappy about leaving their old school.
examples.cn: 孩子们对离开原来的学校很不高兴。

examples.en: She had an unhappy year before the family moved.
examples.cn: 搬家前那一年她过得很不快乐。

examples.en: He smiled unhappily and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他不快地笑了笑，什么也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺哈皮」——俺以为会哈皮一整天，结果一个人待着，怎么也乐不起来。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ happy，happy 源自古诺斯语 happ（机遇、运气），中世纪由「好运」转义为「快乐」

sensesIntro.en: One denied luck covers a sad mood, a complaint, a joyless time, and a clumsy phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份被否定的运气，覆盖低落的心情、抱怨、无乐的时光与失当的措辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: candles burning down in front of a face that cannot smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜡烛烧着，脸上却笑不起来。

branches.en: The mood branch: a long stretch of low feeling.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：一段漫长的低落。

branches.en: The complaint branch: disappointment with a decision.
branches.cn: 抱怨分支：对某个决定的不满。

branches.en: The relationship branch: years with more sorrow than joy.
branches.cn: 关系分支：悲多于喜的年月。

branches.en: The chance branch: the old sense of an unlucky turn.
branches.cn: 机缘分支：运气不佳的古老义。

branches.en: The wording branch: a phrase that does not fit.
branches.cn: 措辞分支：不合宜的说法。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective that came from a Norse word for luck.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个来自诺斯语「运气」的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: A miserable week followed the loss.
items.exampleCN: 失去之后是一周痛苦的日子。

items.example: Customers were dissatisfied with the delay.

definition_zh: 不重要的；无关紧要的；无足轻重的；微不足道的
definition_en: having little or no effect, value, or significance
core_image: 一堆文件里，最上面那张便签没人翻到过
scene: 会议开到一半，主持人在便签上写下的那条小字始终没人提起。The detail seemed unimportant at the time.
sceneCN: 这里 unimportant 是「无关紧要的」（第 1 个义项：影响或价值极小）；句意为这个细节当时看起来无关紧要。没人翻到的便签正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 无足轻重的；微不足道的

collocations.zh: 认为某事不重要而不予理会

derivatives.zh: 形容词去掉 -ant 的名词形式，义为「不重要；无足轻重」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「重要的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「重要性」
词族动词，义为「进口；意味」

senses.title: Having little effect
senses.definition: having little or no effect on what happens
senses.definitionCN: 对事情的发展几乎没有影响
senses.example: Whether the meeting starts ten minutes early is unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 会议早开十分钟与否无关紧要。
senses.why: Import means to carry weight or meaning, so unimportant marks what carries none.
senses.whyCN: import 有「有分量、有意义」之义，因此 unimportant 标记那些毫无分量的东西。

senses.title: Small in value or status
senses.definition: having low rank or little standing among others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之中地位低微、无足轻重
senses.example: He held an unimportant post in the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在部里担任一个无足轻重的职位。
senses.why: Weight in the mind becomes weight in the world, and lightness of weight means low standing.
senses.whyCN: 心中的分量会变成世上的分量，「无重量」便是地位低微。

senses.title: Too small to matter
senses.definition: used of a sum, a detail, or a fault too slight to matter
senses.definitionCN: 形容金额、细节或缺陷太小而无所谓
senses.example: They argued over a sum that was completely unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为一笔完全微不足道的款子争了起来。
senses.why: A thing that cannot tip the balance is unimportant, whichever scale is used.
senses.whyCN: 无论用哪杆秤，压不动天平的东西都不重要。

senses.title: Deliberately set aside
senses.definition: used when someone rates something as not worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 用于某人认定某事不值得关注时
senses.example: She swept the warning aside as unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那警告当作不重要而搁在一边。
senses.why: The word judges from a point of view, so it often reports how someone rates a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是从某个角度看问题，因此常用来转述某人如何评价一件事。

senses.title: Costing little attention or effort
senses.definition: used of tasks that need very little of one attention
senses.definitionCN: 形容只需要很少注意力的任务
senses.example: Filing is an unimportant job but it has to be done.
senses.exampleCN: 归档是件次要的活儿，但总得有人做。
senses.why: What carries no weight can also be carried with one hand, so it needs little effort.
senses.whyCN: 没有分量的东西一只手就能拿，所以也不费什么力气。

intro.en: Import came into English from Latin through French, and the negative adjective was formed in English.
intro.cn: import 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，否定形容词则是英语自己造的。

items.en: Importare meant to bring in, from in- and portare, to carry.
items.cn: importare 意为「带入」，由 in- 与 portare（搬运）构成。

items.en: Importer passed the verb into French with the sense of bringing in goods.
items.cn: importer 把动词带入法语，意为「运进货物」。

items.en: English borrowed import, which grew a sense of carrying meaning or weight.
items.cn: 英语借入 import，并衍生出「有含义、有分量」的意思。

items.en: The adjective important names what carries weight in the mind.
items.cn: 形容词 important 指在心中占有分量的东西。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to important to mark what carries none.
items.cn: 在 important 前加 un-，标记没有分量的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the import family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of smallness.
note.cn: 形近组是 import 词族，近义组汇集表示渺小的词。

normalIntro.en: The word denies carrying weight, and portare, to carry, is the hidden root.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定了「有分量」的搬运，而搬运的词根 portare 就藏在里面。

normal.en: Un- plus important: not carrying weight.
normal.cn: un- 加 important：无分量。

normal.en: Seem unimportant is the frame for a story that turns out badly.
normal.cn: seem unimportant 是那种事后出事的叙事的常用框架。

normal.en: Importance is the noun, and importantly is the sentence adverb.
normal.cn: importance 是名词，importantly 是句子副词。

normal.en: Import, transport, and portable share the carrying root portare.
normal.cn: import、transport 与 portable 共用「搬运」词根 portare。

normal.en: People often prefer not important to unimportant in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中人们常更愿意说 not important 而不是 unimportant。

abstract.en: Picture a sticky note on top of a file that nobody opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠文件上那张没人打开看的便签。

abstract.en: See a small name at the bottom of a long list.
abstract.cn: 看一长串名单末尾那个小名字。

abstract.en: Hear a warning that everyone nods at and forgets.
abstract.cn: 听一句人人点头忘却的警告。

examples.en: A detail that looked unimportant later solved the case.
examples.cn: 一个当时看似无关紧要的细节后来破了大案。

examples.en: Her role in the firm is not unimportant.
examples.cn: 她在公司里的角色并非无足轻重。

examples.en: They wasted an hour arguing about unimportant matters.
examples.cn: 他们为一个不重要的问题争论了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺 unimportant」——俺在这堆事里，就像纸角上那行小字，谁也不会多看一眼。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ important，important 由拉丁语 importare（带入）经法语 importer 演变而来，词根 portare 意为「搬运」

sensesIntro.en: The absence of weight explains why nothing here matters: no effect, no status, no size, no attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 缺少分量解释了这里为何一切都不重要：无影响、无地位、无体量、无需注意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small note that nobody ever turns to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张始终没人翻到的便签。

branches.en: The effect branch: a detail that changes nothing.
branches.cn: 影响分支：改变不了任何事的细节。

branches.en: The status branch: a post of little standing.
branches.cn: 地位分支：地位低微的职位。

branches.en: The size branch: a sum too small to count.
branches.cn: 大小分支：小到不必计算的数额。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a person rating it low.
branches.cn: 评判分支：某人把它评为不重要。

branches.en: The effort branch: a task that asks little.
branches.cn: 用力分支：要求不高的任务。

intro.en: An English prefix on a French adjective built from a Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: 英语前缀压在一个法语形容词上，而它由拉丁语「搬运」动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Portare is the carrying root shared by import, transport, and export.
latinIntro.cn: portare 是「搬运」词根，import、transport、export 共用。

items.example: A trivial error cost them the match.
items.exampleCN: 一个小失误让他们输掉了比赛。

definition_zh: 联合；结合；工会；联盟；同盟；团结
definition_en: the joining of separate parts into one, or an organization formed by such a joining
core_image: 两只手握在一起，指尖扣得紧紧的
scene: 十几家小作坊的师傅在一张桌前签下同一份章程，从此一起谈价钱。The craftsmen formed a union to protect their trade.
sceneCN: 这里 union 是「工会」（第 2 个义项：由联合而成的组织）；句意为工匠们结成了一个行会来维护本行。两只紧握的手，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合；团结」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
动词加 -ed 的形容词，义为「联合的；一致的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: The act of joining into one
senses.definition: the joining of two or more things so that they become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多事物结合成一体的过程
senses.example: The bridge is a happy union of steel and glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是钢与玻璃的巧妙结合。
senses.why: The Latin unus, one, plus the noun ending io, gives the idea of making one out of several.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus（一）加名词词尾 io，给出「把多个变成一」的意思。

senses.title: An organization of workers
senses.definition: an organization of employees who act together over pay and conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为工资与工作条件共同行动的雇员组织
senses.example: The union asked for a shorter working week.
senses.exampleCN: 工会要求缩短每周工作时间。
senses.why: Workers who speak with one voice are joined into one body, and the body takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 用一个声音说话的工人被联结成一个整体，而这个整体直接取得了这个名字。

senses.title: A league of states or groups
senses.definition: a political or trade alliance in which separate parts keep some of their own powers
senses.definitionCN: 各部分保留部分自主权的政治或经济联盟
senses.example: The two countries signed a customs union in 1957.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在 1957 年签订了一个关税同盟。
senses.why: Joining for a purpose without melting completely is the political version of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 为了某个目的结合而不完全融为一体，是同一幅画面的政治版本。

senses.title: Harmony between people
senses.definition: a state of agreement and love between people or within a group
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间或群体内部的和谐与情谊
senses.example: The couple lived in union for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻和睦地生活了五十年。
senses.why: When separate lives hold together, the union is a bond rather than an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当各自的生活握在一起，这个 union 就是一种纽带，而不是机构。

senses.title: A place where students gather
senses.definition: used in names of student organizations or their buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用于学生组织或其活动场所的名称
senses.example: They met at the student union and planned the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在学生会见面，筹划了那场音乐会。
senses.why: A building named after the joining of students is simply the institution turned into a place.
senses.whyCN: 以学生之联合命名的场所，不过是把机构变成了具体的地方。

intro.en: The word goes back to Latin unio, oneness, from unus, one.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语 unio（一体），源自 unus（一）。

items.en: Unio meant oneness, and also named a single large pearl.
items.cn: unio 意为「一体」，也指一颗大珍珠。

items.en: The word entered French as union with the sense of combining.
items.cn: 该词进入法语作 union，含「结合」之义。

items.en: English used union for the joining of things, people, and realms.
items.cn: 英语用 union 表示物、人与人乃至王国的结合。

items.en: From the eighteenth century it named associations of workers or traders.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，它用来指工人或商人的组织。

items.en: In politics it appears in the names of alliances and federal states.
items.cn: 在政治中，它出现于联盟与联邦国家的名称里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers uni- words, and the near-meaning group covers leagues and harmony.
note.cn: 形近组收集 uni- 开头的词，近义组覆盖联盟与和谐的说法。

entries.definition: a formal agreement to act together
a group of teams or states

normalIntro.en: One root, one, sits under the union, the unit, and the united.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，撑起 union、unit 与 united。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -ion makes a noun of the joining.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-ion 把这种结合变作名词。

normal.en: Trade union is the British phrase; labor union is the American one.
normal.cn: trade union 是英式说法，labor union 是美式说法。

normal.en: Unity is the state, union is the act or the body.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，union 是行为或那个实体。

normal.en: United appears in country names that grew out of unions.
normal.cn: 许多国家名里的 united 正出自这样的联合。

normal.en: The same root gives unit, unite, and unique.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还生出 unit、unite 与 unique。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped with fingers locked.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手指紧扣的手。

abstract.en: See dozens of small workshops putting one stamp on a single sheet.
abstract.cn: 看几十家小作坊在同一张纸上盖下同一个印。

abstract.en: Hear a hall of voices agreeing on a single sentence.
abstract.cn: 听满厅的声音在同一句话上达成一致。

examples.en: The union of the two firms created the largest bank in the region.
examples.cn: 两家公司的合并造就了本地区最大的银行。

examples.en: Union members voted to accept the new pay offer.
examples.cn: 工会会员投票接受了新的薪酬方案。

examples.en: Their marriage was a union of two very different families.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻是两个差异极大的家庭的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼昂」——尤尼（一）加昂（上），大家往一个方向上凑，就是联合。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）+ 名词词尾 -io 构成 unio（一体），经古法语 union 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root, one, gives the act of joining, the body formed, the league, the bond, and the building.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，给出结合的行为、形成的实体、联盟、纽带与场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands clasped with fingers locked.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手指紧扣的手。

branches.en: The act branch: things joined into a new whole.
branches.cn: 行为分支：事物联结成新的整体。

branches.en: The workers branch: one voice for many employees.
branches.cn: 劳工分支：众多雇员共用一个声音。

branches.en: The state branch: separate parts under one flag.
branches.cn: 国家分支：各部分共处一面旗帜之下。

branches.en: The bond branch: lives held together in harmony.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：和谐中相依的生活。

branches.en: The place branch: a building named after the joining.
branches.cn: 场所分支：以这种联合命名的建筑。

intro.en: The word is a Latin number plus a noun ending, carried through French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语数词加名词词尾，经由法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unio are the Latin sources, and uni- recurs across the family.
latinIntro.cn: unus 与 unio 是拉丁语来源，uni- 在这一族里反复出现。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: Union names the act of making one.
items.exampleCN: union 指合而为一的行为。

items.example: Unity names the state of being one.
Alliance and union are near twins.
items.exampleCN: alliance 与 union 是近邻。

items.example: A league of towns met each spring.
items.exampleCN: 各镇组成的联盟每年春天集会。

definition_zh: 单位；单元；部件；部队小单位；一元（计量的量）
definition_en: a single thing or group treated as one whole, especially in measuring or organizing
core_image: 一盒积木被分成一块一块，每块都算一个
scene: 装修师傅在图纸上把一间病房划成几个格子，每个格子单独计价。The flat is divided into three units.
sceneCN: 这里 unit 是「单元」（第 1 个义项：被当作整体的一个部分）；句意为这套房子被分成三个单元。积木一块一块各算一个，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合；团结」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
同根形容词，义为「单一的；统一的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: A single part counted as one
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a larger whole is divided for counting or planning
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体为计数或规划而划分出的一个部分
senses.example: The course is divided into twelve units.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课分成十二个单元。
senses.why: The root means one, so a unit is whatever is being counted as one.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「一」，因此 unit 就是被算作「一个」的那个东西。

senses.title: A fixed amount used in measuring
senses.definition: a standard quantity used to express measurements
senses.definitionCN: 用于表达测量结果的标准量
senses.example: The metre is a unit of length.
senses.exampleCN: 米是长度单位。
senses.why: Measuring means chopping a continuous thing into countable ones, and each piece is a unit.
senses.whyCN: 测量就是把连续的量切成可数的一个个，每一个就是 unit。

senses.title: A piece of equipment or furniture
senses.definition: one item of equipment, or a piece that forms part of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 一台设备，或构成机器一部分的组件
senses.example: The cooling unit needs replacing every three years.
senses.exampleCN: 冷却装置每三年要更换一次。
senses.why: Machines are built from countable one-pieces, and the pieces keep the name.
senses.whyCN: 机器由可数的「一个个」拼成，这些部件也沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A small group in an organization
senses.definition: a group that works as one body, especially in an army or hospital
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体行动的小组，尤指军队或医院中的
senses.example: A medical unit was sent to the mountain village.
senses.exampleCN: 一支医疗队被派往那个山村。
senses.why: Several people acting as one are, from outside, a single unit.
senses.whyCN: 几个人如同一个人那样行动，从外面看就是一个 unit。

senses.title: A private flat or building section
senses.definition: one separate living space or workshop within a larger building
senses.definitionCN: 较大建筑内一个独立的居住空间或车间
senses.example: They rented a small unit above the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们租了车库上方的一个小单元。
senses.why: A building can be cut into countable spaces, each of which stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 一栋房子可以被切成一个个可数的空间，每个空间各自独立。

intro.en: The word is a contraction of the Latin word for one, first used in English by mathematicians.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「一」的缩略形式，最早由英语中的数学家用起来。

items.en: Unus meant one, and unitas meant oneness.
items.cn: unus 意为「一」，unitas 意为「一体」。

items.en: English writers formed unit from the Latin root for use in arithmetic.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者用这个拉丁词根造出 unit，用于算术。

items.en: It spread from numbers to any single part counted as one.
items.cn: 它从数字扩展到任何被算作一个的部分。

items.en: Military and medical units gave it an organizational sense.
items.cn: 军队与医疗机构中的 unit 赋予了它组织层面的意义。

items.en: Housing units and industrial units bring it into everyday building language.
items.cn: 住房单元与工业厂房单元让它进入日常的建筑语言。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the uni- family, and the near-meaning group covers parts and measures.
note.cn: 形近组是 uni- 词族，近义组覆盖部分与度量单位的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 解开（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a part of a larger whole
a unit or system for measuring

normalIntro.en: Everything here is one thing counted as one, whether a lesson, a metre, or a clinic team.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的一切都是被算作「一个」的东西，无论是一课、一米，还是一支医疗队。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and the word names one countable piece.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，这个词就指一个可数的部分。

normal.en: A unit of measurement is the phrase used in science lessons.
normal.cn: a unit of measurement 是科学课上用的说法。

normal.en: Unit price on a shop label tells you the cost of one item.
normal.cn: 商店标签上的 unit price 指单件的价钱。

normal.en: Unite is the verb, unity the state, unitarity the quality of being one.
normal.cn: unite 是动词，unity 是状态，unitarity 是一体的性质。

normal.en: Housing unit and industrial unit turn the word into a piece of property.
normal.cn: housing unit 与 industrial unit 让这个词变成一处房产。

abstract.en: Picture a row of building blocks, each one separate.
abstract.cn: 想象一排积木，每一块都独立。

abstract.en: See a ruler marked with even black lines.
abstract.cn: 看一把尺子上一道道匀称的黑线。

abstract.en: Hear a doctor say a team of four will come up the hill.
abstract.cn: 听医生说一支四人的小队会上山来。

examples.en: The factory produces a thousand units a week.
examples.cn: 这家工厂每周生产一千台设备。

examples.en: Kilogram is the base unit of mass in the metric system.
examples.cn: 千克是公制中的基本质量单位。

examples.en: Each unit in the block has its own small garden.
examples.cn: 这排房屋的每个单元都有自己的小花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼特」——尤尼是「一」，特指其中一份，就是一个单位。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）的缩略形式，十六世纪英语借此词根造出 unit，用于算术与计量

sensesIntro.en: One countable piece works as a lesson, a metre, a machine part, a team, and a flat.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个可数的部分，既是一课、一米，也是零件、小队与一套房。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box of blocks separated into single pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盒积木被分成一块一块。

branches.en: The counting branch: one part of a larger whole.
branches.cn: 计数分支：较大整体中的一个部分。

branches.en: The measuring branch: the standard chop of a quantity.
branches.cn: 度量分支：量被切成的标准份。

branches.en: The equipment branch: one machine or one part.
branches.cn: 设备分支：一台机器或一个部件。

branches.en: The staffing branch: people who act as one.
branches.cn: 人员分支：如同一个人行动的一群人。

branches.en: The property branch: a space that stands alone.
branches.cn: 房产分支：独立存在的一处空间。

intro.en: A Latin root for one plus a short noun ending is all this word contains.
intro.cn: 表示「一」的拉丁词根加一个短名词词尾，就是这个词的全部。

latinIntro.en: Unus is the source, and unitas gives the abstract noun unity.
latinIntro.cn: unus 是源头，unitas 生出抽象名词 unity。
