definition_zh: 联合；团结；使结合；合并；团结一致
definition_en: to join together so as to form a single whole or act as one
core_image: 两条河在山脚汇成一条，水色也混在一起
scene: 洪水冲垮了桥，村里几家人合起来合力搭了一座木桥。The villagers united to rebuild the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 unite 是「团结起来、联合」（第 1 个义项：使结合为一个整体）；句意为村民们联合起来重建桥梁。两条河汇作一条，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ed 的形容词，义为「联合的；团结的」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
由 unify 加后缀的名词，义为「统一；一体化」

senses.title: To join into one body
senses.definition: to come or bring together so that separate parts form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 分开的部分走到一起，形成一个整体
senses.example: The two parties united to form a single government.
senses.exampleCN: 两党联合组成了一个政府。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind union: making one out of several.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词正是 union 背后的动作：把几个变成一。

senses.title: To stand together for a purpose
senses.definition: to act together with others in support of or against something
senses.definitionCN: 为支持或反对某事而与他人共同行动
senses.example: The whole town united against the closing of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇团结起来反对关闭那所学校。
senses.why: Being one body becomes being one voice, which is what the preposition against marks.
senses.whyCN: 成为一个整体，就变成了一个声音，against 正标记这一点。

senses.title: To bring qualities together in one thing
senses.definition: to combine different qualities or features in a single person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的品质或特点集于一人一物之中
senses.example: The design unites beauty with strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计兼具美观与坚固。
senses.why: What can be joined in the world can also be joined in a description.
senses.whyCN: 世间能合起来的，在描述里也能合起来。

senses.title: To bring people into harmony
senses.definition: to end division and bring people back into agreement
senses.definitionCN: 结束分裂，使人重新达成一致
senses.example: The loss united the family in a way nothing else could.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失去以别的方式无法做到的方式把这个家团结了起来。
senses.why: A single whole is also a peaceful one, so the verb carries the sense of harmony.
senses.whyCN: 一个整体也是一个和平的整体，因此这个动词带着和睦的意味。

senses.title: A nation under one flag
senses.definition: to bring regions into a single state or under one rule
senses.definitionCN: 把各地区合为一个国家或置于同一统治之下
senses.example: The leader united the scattered provinces into one country.
senses.exampleCN: 这位领袖把分散的诸省统一成一个国家。
senses.why: Political unity is the same joining at the scale of a country.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的统一不过是同一件事在国家尺度上的表现。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin unitus, the past participle of unire, to make one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 unitus，即 unire（使成一体）的过去分词。

items.en: Unire meant to make one, from unus, one.
items.cn: unire 意为「使成一体」，出自 unus（一）。

items.en: The verb passed into French with the sense of coming together.
items.cn: 该动词进入法语，含「聚在一起」的意思。

items.en: English adopted unite for both joining and bringing agreement.
items.cn: 英语采用 unite，兼表结合与促成一致。

items.en: Pressure forms such as united front made it a political word.
items.cn: united front 之类的说法让它成为政治词汇。

items.en: It appears in many country names that grew from union.
items.cn: 它出现在许多由联合而来的国名里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers uni- family members, and the near-meaning group covers joining words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 uni- 词族成员，近义组覆盖表示结合的词。

entries.definition: a joining or a workers body

entries.definition: to become one company or thing

normalIntro.en: The verb is the doing behind the noun union: turning several into one.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词是名词 union 背后的动作：把几个变一。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -te marks the verb of making one.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-te 标记「使成一体」的动词。

normal.en: Unite against is the pattern for common enemies.
normal.cn: unite against 是面对共同敌人时的常用结构。

normal.en: United appears in the names of countries formed by joining.
normal.cn: united 出现在由联合而来的国名中。

normal.en: Unity is the state, union the body or the act, unite the deed.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，union 是实体或行为，unite 则是动作。

normal.en: Design unites beauty with strength is a common written pattern.
normal.cn: 「design unites beauty with strength」是常见的书面句型。

abstract.en: Picture two rivers meeting and running on as one.
abstract.cn: 想象两条河汇合后一起流。

abstract.en: See strangers passing buckets along a line to a fire.
abstract.cn: 看陌生人排成一列传递水桶去救火。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd break into one song.
abstract.cn: 听人群忽然唱成同一首歌。

examples.en: The workers united to demand safer conditions.
examples.cn: 工人们联合起来要求更安全的工作条件。

examples.en: Her speech united the room in a way no one expected.
examples.cn: 她的讲话以出人意料的方式让全场团结起来。

examples.en: The plan unites the old station with a modern glass hall.
examples.cn: 这个方案把老车站与现代化的玻璃大厅结合在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤奈特」——尤尼是「一」，特指这一回，大家凑成一伙就是联合。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）→ unire（使成一体）的过去分词 unitus，经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers joining bodies, standing together, blending qualities, healing division, and unifying a country.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词覆盖联合实体、并肩而立、融合品质、弥合分裂与统一国家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rivers running on as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条河汇成一条继续流。

branches.en: The joining branch: two parties becoming one body.
branches.cn: 结合分支：两方成为一个实体。

branches.en: The action branch: standing together over a cause.
branches.cn: 行动分支：为了一个目标并肩而立。

branches.en: The blending branch: qualities held in one thing.
branches.cn: 融合分支：品质集于一身。

branches.en: The harmony branch: division ended, agreement restored.
branches.cn: 和睦分支：分裂结束，重归一致。

branches.en: The national branch: provinces brought under one rule.
branches.cn: 国家分支：诸省归于一个政权。

intro.en: A Latin root for one plus a verb ending gives the action of making one.
intro.cn: 表示「一」的拉丁词根加动词词尾，给出「使成一体」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Unire, from unus, is the Latin source; unity and union share it.
latinIntro.cn: unire 出自 unus，是拉丁语来源，unity 与 union 同出这一词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: Union names the act of joining.
The treaty unifies the two systems.

definition_zh: 联合的；团结的；一致的；（诸国）联合而成的
definition_en: joined together or acting as one, especially in purpose
core_image: 一队人并肩拉着同一根绳
scene: 拔河那天下着雨，一队人也一步没退，绳子上的红布稳稳停在原地。The team stood united to the end.
sceneCN: 这里 united 是「团结一致的」（第 1 个义项：作为一个整体行动）；句意为这队人始终团结到最后。并肩拉同一根绳，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词的原形动词，义为「联合」
同根名词，义为「团结」
同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
同根动词 unify 加后缀的名词，义为「统一；一体化」

senses.title: Acting as one body
senses.definition: working together with a single aim, without division
senses.definitionCN: 同心协力、没有分歧地一起做事
senses.example: The party remained united after the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之后，该党依然团结。
senses.why: The past participle of unite tells you the joining is already done and now describes the body.
senses.whyCN: unite 的过去分词说明联结已经完成，如今用来形容那个整体。

senses.title: Formed by joining parts
senses.definition: made by bringing separate parts or areas into one organization or state
senses.definitionCN: 由分开的部分或地区合成一个组织或国家
senses.example: The United Kingdom was formed over several centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 联合王国是经几个世纪逐步形成的。
senses.why: A name that records the joining keeps the participle, as in the United Nations.
senses.whyCN: 记录这次联结的名称保留了分词形式，如 the United Nations。

senses.title: Held in common by a group
senses.definition: used to describe an effort or attitude shared by all concerned
senses.definitionCN: 形容所有相关方共同拥有的努力或态度
senses.example: They made a united effort to save the library.
senses.exampleCN: 他们共同努力保住了那间图书馆。
senses.why: What all share at once is exactly what makes a group one body.
senses.whyCN: 所有人同时拥有的，正是让一个群体成为一体的东西。

senses.title: Standing together despite pressure
senses.titleCN: 稳而不散的（应对压力时）
senses.definition: used when people hold together under attack or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们在受攻击或遇难处时仍然齐心
senses.example: The town stayed united through the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇在艰难的那个冬天里始终不散。
senses.why: A body that does not come apart under strain shows the joining most clearly.
senses.whyCN: 在拉扯下不散的整体，最能显示那次联结。

senses.title: Joined in marriage or partnership
senses.definition: used formally of two people joined for life or for business
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法，指两人结为终身伴侣或生意伙伴
senses.example: The two architects have been united in one practice for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位建筑师多年来合开同一间事务所。
senses.why: The same image of one body applies to people who bind their lives or work.
senses.whyCN: 「一个身体」的意象，同样用在与他人结成生活或事业的人身上。

intro.en: The form is the past participle of unite, whose root is Latin unire, to make one.
intro.cn: 这个词形是 unite 的过去分词，其词根是拉丁语 unire（使成一体）。

items.en: Unire, from unus, meant to make one.
items.cn: unire 出自 unus，意为使成一体。

items.en: French developed the participle form that English later borrowed.
items.cn: 法语发展出分词形式，英语后来借入。

items.en: United appeared in English descriptions of joined groups.
items.cn: united 出现在英语中描写联合群体的文字里。

items.en: It became standard in names of states formed by union.
items.cn: 它成为由联合形成的国家名称中的标准用词。

items.en: The United Nations borrowed the same participle in 1945.
items.cn: 1945 年，联合国沿用了同一个分词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds unite family forms, and the near-meaning group covers harmony words.
note.cn: 形近组是 unite 词族的形式，近义组覆盖表示和谐的词。

entries.definition: a joining or a workers body

entries.definitionCN: 未被邀请的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The ending -ed says the joining is finished, so the word describes a body that is already one.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -ed 说明联结已经完成，因此这个词形容的是一个已经合一的整体。

normal.en: United is the past participle of unite used as an adjective.
normal.cn: united 是 unite 的过去分词作形容词。

normal.en: Stand united is the most common short pattern in speeches.
normal.cn: stand united 是演讲中最常见的简短说法。

normal.en: The United Nations and the United Kingdom record historic joinings.
normal.cn: 联合国与联合王国的名称记录了历史性的联合。

normal.en: A united effort means an effort shared by all.
normal.cn: a united effort 指所有人共同的努力。

normal.en: Unity is the state; united describes those who hold it.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，united 则形容拥有这种状态的人。

abstract.en: Picture a tug-of-war rope held by hands that do not shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被许多手握住、纹丝不动的拔河绳。

abstract.en: See a row of shields overlapping without a gap.
abstract.cn: 看一排盾牌交叠，没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Hear a vote called and answered by one voice.
abstract.cn: 听一次表决被同一个声音回应。

examples.en: The family stayed united after the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关门后，这个家依然齐心。

examples.en: They presented a united front to the press.
examples.cn: 他们向媒体呈现出一个统一的阵线。

examples.en: The United Nations was founded in 1945.
examples.cn: 联合国成立于 1945 年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤奈替德」——尤奈是「一」，替德是「得到」，大家得到同一个心，就是团结。

root: unite 的过去分词，unite 源自拉丁语 unus（一）与 unire（使成一体），经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One finished joining describes a team, a shared effort, a name, a marriage, and a body under strain.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次已完成的联结，形容团队、共同付出、国名、婚姻与承压不散的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people pulling the same rope and not shifting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人拉同一根绳，一步不退。

branches.en: The body branch: a group that acts without division.
branches.cn: 整体分支：没有分歧地行动的一群。

branches.en: The name branch: states and bodies formed by joining.
branches.cn: 名称分支：由联合形成的国家与机构。

branches.en: The effort branch: something all concerned share.
branches.cn: 努力分支：所有相关方共同之举。

branches.en: The strain branch: holding together through difficulty.
branches.cn: 压力分支：在难处中不散。

branches.en: The bond branch: two lives or firms joined formally.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：两种生活或两家机构的正式结合。

intro.en: A Latin root for one, a verb ending, and a participle ending make the whole word.
intro.cn: 表示「一」的拉丁词根、动词词尾与分词词尾，构成整个词。

latinIntro.en: Unire comes from unus, and unity and union are its close relatives.
latinIntro.cn: unire 出自 unus，unity 与 union 则是它的近亲。

items.exampleCN: 这些团体每年春天联合。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀

items.example: A harmonious choir is united in sound.
items.exampleCN: 和谐的合唱团声音如一。

definition_zh: 团结；统一；整体；协调；同一性（艺术、逻辑中）
definition_en: the state of being one, joined, or in agreement
core_image: 一张网上的许多结，都连着同一根主线
scene: 排练的时候，二十几把小提琴的弓角度一致，声音像一片。The orchestra played with remarkable unity.
sceneCN: 这里 unity 是「协调一致」（第 1 个义项：作为整体的一）；句意为乐团演奏得异常协调。许多结都连着同一根主线，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合」
同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
同根形容词，义为「统一的；单一的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: The state of being one
senses.definition: the condition of being joined into a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 合成为一个整体的状态
senses.example: The unity of the two halves was never fully achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 这两半始终没能真正合为一体。
senses.why: The Latin root unus, one, plus -itas names the state of being one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 unus（一）加 -itas，命名的正是「是一体」的状态。

senses.title: Agreement among people
senses.definition: the condition of people agreeing and acting together
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此一致、共同行动的状况
senses.example: The speech called for unity in a divided country.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲话呼吁分裂的国家团结起来。
senses.why: People who agree are one in purpose, so the same word serves for social harmony.
senses.whyCN: 意见一致的人在目的上是同一个，因此这个词也用于社会和睦。

senses.title: Harmony of parts in a work
senses.definition: the quality in a work that makes its parts belong together
senses.definitionCN: 让作品的各部分显得同属一体的品质
senses.example: The painting has a unity of colour that holds the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画在色彩上有一种统一感，把目光留在画里。
senses.why: Judging a work means checking whether its pieces return to one shape.
senses.whyCN: 评判一件作品，就是在看它的各个部分是否回到同一个形状。

senses.title: Singleness of aim
senses.definition: used of a shared purpose that directs a group
senses.definitionCN: 形容指引一个群体的共同目的
senses.example: The campaign was run with unity of purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动的推进目标一致。
senses.why: One aim is the practical shape of oneness in a working group.
senses.whyCN: 一个目标，是一体性在工作群体中的实际形态。

senses.title: Sameness in logic or mathematics
senses.definition: in technical use, the fact of being a single entity or value
senses.definitionCN: 在技术用法中，指为单一实体或单一数值
senses.example: The law of identity rests on the unity of a thing with itself.
senses.exampleCN: 同一律建立在事物与自身的一体性之上。
senses.why: The oldest philosophical question is whether one thing is really one, and unity names that.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的哲学问题就是一个事物是否真为「一」，而 unity 正是这件事的名字。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin unitas, oneness, built on unus, one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 unitas（一体），建立在 unus（一）之上。

items.en: Unus meant one, and unitas named the state of being one.
items.cn: unus 意为「一」，unitas 则是「一体」的状态。

items.en: The word passed into French and then into English.
items.cn: 该词经法语传入英语。

items.en: English used unity for religious and social oneness.
items.cn: 英语用 unity 表示宗教与社会的一体。

items.en: Political writing made unity a standard word for agreement.
items.cn: 政治写作使 unity 成为表示一致的标准用词。

items.en: Criticism borrowed it for harmony in art and music.
items.cn: 文艺批评借它表示艺术与音乐中的协调。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the uni- family, and the near-meaning group covers harmony and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组是 uni- 词族，近义组覆盖和谐与一致的说法。

entries.definition: a joining or a workers body

entries.definitionCN: 不寻常的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun of oneness, so it covers a body, a crowd, a picture, and a purpose.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一体」的名词，因此覆盖整体、人群、画面与目标。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -ty names the state.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-ty 命名的是那种状态。

normal.en: National unity is the phrase you meet in newspapers.
normal.cn: national unity 是报纸上常见的说法。

normal.en: Unity of purpose is a fixed phrase for shared aims.
normal.cn: unity of purpose 是表示共同目标的固定说法。

normal.en: Unity is uncountable, unlike union.
normal.cn: 与 union 不同，unity 不可数。

normal.en: Unite is the act, union the body, unity the condition.
normal.cn: unite 是动作，union 是实体，unity 是状况。

abstract.en: Picture many threads tied to a single line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多线系在同一根主线上。

abstract.en: See a choir breathe together before the first word.
abstract.cn: 看合唱团在第一个字前一起吸气。

abstract.en: Hear a hall agree without a single voice raised.
abstract.cn: 听满厅一致，没有一个人出声反对。

examples.en: The new leader promised to restore unity to the party.
examples.cn: 这位新领袖承诺让党内恢复团结。

examples.en: There is a striking unity between the two designs.
examples.cn: 两个设计之间有惊人的一致性。

examples.en: The novel is admired for the unity of its structure.
examples.cn: 这部小说的结构统一性为人称道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼替」——尤尼是「一」，替是「替上」，众人替成一个，就是团结。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）+ 名词词尾 -itas 构成 unitas（一体），经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One state, being one, appears as a whole, a crowd, a work of art, a shared aim, and a logical value.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种状态，是一体，表现为整体、人群、艺术作品、共同目标与逻辑上的单一。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many threads knotted to the same main line.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多根线都系在同一根主线上。

branches.en: The whole branch: parts that have become one thing.
branches.cn: 整体分支：合成一物的各部分。

branches.en: The crowd branch: people in agreement.
branches.cn: 人群分支：意见一致的人们。

branches.en: The artwork branch: colour and form that hold together.
branches.cn: 作品分支：色彩与形式相守。

branches.en: The purpose branch: a single aim guiding a group.
branches.cn: 目标分支：指引群体的单一目标。

branches.en: The logical branch: the sameness of a thing with itself.
branches.cn: 逻辑分支：事物与自身同一。

intro.en: A Latin number plus a noun suffix for state gives the abstract word.
intro.cn: 拉丁语数词加表示状态的名词后缀，得到这个抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unitas are the Latin sources for unity, unite, and union.
latinIntro.cn: unus 与 unitas 是 unity、unite、union 的拉丁来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态的拉丁语后缀

items.example: Union is the act and the body.
Harmony and unity are close twins.
items.exampleCN: harmony 与 unity 是近亲。

items.example: Solidarity is shared feeling, unity is one state.
items.exampleCN: solidarity 是共同情感，unity 是一体状态。

definition_zh: 不寻常地；特别地；异常地；非常
definition_en: more than is usual, or in a way that is not common
core_image: 整条街都安静，只有一扇窗还亮着灯
scene: 三月里竟下起了雪，院子里那株桃树的花全被压低了。It snowed unusually late this year.
sceneCN: 这里 unusually 是「异常地、不寻常地」（第 1 个义项：超出常态）；句意为今年下雪下得反常地晚。整条街只有一扇窗亮着，正是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 非常；特别（放在形容词前）

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不寻常的」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「通常的」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「通常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不寻常」

senses.title: More than normal in degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say the degree is greater than usual
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明程度超出平常
senses.example: The winter was unusually mild this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的冬天反常地温和。
senses.why: The prefix negates usual, and before an adjective the word simply marks a degree that departs from the norm.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 usual（通常的），放在形容词前时，这个词只标记一种偏离常态的程度。

senses.title: In a way that is not common
senses.definition: used of behaviour or events that rarely happen
senses.definitionCN: 形容罕见的行为或事件
senses.example: She was unusually silent during dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭时她异常沉默。
senses.why: What departs from the usual way also departs from the usual amount.
senses.whyCN: 偏离寻常方式的东西，也偏离了寻常的分量。

senses.title: Attached to weather and numbers
senses.definition: used with measurements to signal a figure outside the usual range
senses.definitionCN: 与测量数值连用，表示数字超出通常范围
senses.example: Prices rose unusually fast in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第一季度物价上涨得反常地快。
senses.why: Figures are compared with past figures, so a number off the pattern is called unusual.
senses.whyCN: 数字要和以往比，脱离规律的数字就被称为不寻常。

senses.title: As an intensifier close to very
senses.definition: used informally to mean remarkably or very
senses.definitionCN: 口语中可理解为「非常、格外」
senses.example: He is an unusually patient teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位格外有耐心的老师。
senses.why: Great rarity in degree feels like great strength, so the word drifts towards very.
senses.whyCN: 程度上的罕见感会觉得像强度，于是这个词向 very 靠拢。

senses.title: Before a noun in formal style
senses.definition: sometimes placed before a noun phrase in careful written English
senses.definitionCN: 在讲究的书面英语中有时放在名词短语前
senses.example: An unusually large crowd gathered before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午之前就聚集了格外多的人。
senses.why: Written English likes to hang the comparison directly on the noun it measures.
senses.whyCN: 书面英语喜欢把比较直接挂到被衡量的名词上。

intro.en: The adverb is un- plus usually, with usual coming from Latin usus, use.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 un- 加 usually，而 usual 源自拉丁语 usus（使用）。

items.en: Usus meant use or practice, and usualis described what is customary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、惯例，usualis 则形容「合乎习惯的」。

items.en: The word passed into French and then into English as usual.
items.cn: 该词经法语进入英语，作 usual。

items.en: Usually was formed as an adverb of manner and time.
items.cn: usually 作为方式与时间副词而形成。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to mark what departs from custom.
items.cn: 加 un- 以标记偏离惯例者。

items.en: Before adjectives it has become a familiar intensifier for odd degrees.
items.cn: 放在形容词前，它成了标记异常程度的常用加强词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds usual forms, and the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 usual 的各种形式，近义组汇集表示惊讶的副词。

entries.definition: in a state too broken to use
entries.definitionCN: 无法使用地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: One prefix, one adjective, one adverb ending: the word says what happens off the usual line.
normalIntro.cn: 一个前缀、一个形容词、一个副词词尾：说的就是偏离常态之事。

normal.en: Un- plus usually: not in the usual way or measure.
normal.cn: un- 加 usually：不是通常的方式或分量。

normal.en: It most often sits directly before an adjective: unusually warm.
normal.cn: 它最常直接放在形容词前：unusually warm。

normal.en: Unusual is the adjective, unusually the adverb, unusualness the noun.
normal.cn: 形容词是 unusual，副词是 unusually，名词是 unusualness。

normal.en: Usually is the neutral counterpart used for habits.
normal.cn: usually 是中性对应词，用于习惯。

normal.en: In careful writing it can precede a noun phrase with an adjective.
normal.cn: 在讲究的书面语中，它可以置于带形容词的名词短语前。

abstract.en: Picture one lit window on a dark street.
abstract.cn: 想象黑街上只有一扇亮着的窗。

abstract.en: See peach blossom bent down by March snow.
abstract.cn: 看三月飞雪压低了桃花。

abstract.en: Hear a usually noisy child sit through a whole meal in silence.
abstract.cn: 听一个平时吵闹的孩子安静坐着吃完一整顿饭。

examples.en: This spring has been unusually wet.
examples.cn: 今年春天格外多雨。

examples.en: The shop was unusually busy for a Monday.
examples.cn: 对星期一来说，这家店异常忙碌。

examples.en: She spoke unusually softly, as if someone was asleep.
examples.cn: 她说话格外轻，像是有谁睡着了一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺尤淑莉」——平时挺淑女的人，今天格外反常，说话都不一样了。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ usually，usual 源自拉丁语 usus（使用、惯例）与 usualis，经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One departure from what normally happens marks degrees, manners, numbers, and even weather.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对常态的偏离，标记出程度、方式、数字乃至天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lit window on a dark, quiet street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条安静黑街上唯一亮着的窗。

branches.en: The degree branch: warmer, later, or faster than ever.
branches.cn: 程度分支：比往常更暖、更晚、更快。

branches.en: The manner branch: quiet in a way people notice.
branches.cn: 方式分支：安静得让人留意。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers outside the pattern.
branches.cn: 数字分支：脱离规律的数字。

branches.en: The intensifier branch: almost a polite very.
branches.cn: 加强分支：几乎是客气的 very。

branches.en: The written branch: hung before a noun phrase.
branches.cn: 书面分支：挂在名词短语之前。

intro.en: The parts are a negative prefix, a Latin-derived adjective, and the adverb ending.
intro.cn: 部件是否定前缀、源于拉丁语的形容词与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Usus, use, lies under usual, and is shared with use and usage.
latinIntro.cn: usus（使用）藏在 usual 之下，与 use、usage 同源。

items.example: Usual gives usually in noun use.
items.exampleCN: usual 加 -ly 可构成形容词。

items.example: An extraordinarily long day ended late.
items.exampleCN: 异常漫长的一天结束得很晚。

definition_zh: 不仁慈的；不厚道的；刻薄的；不体贴的
definition_en: behaving in a way that is cruel, cold, or hurtful to others
core_image: 伸出去的手被干脆地拨开
scene: 她递东西给父亲，父亲头也没回低声说了句让她走开。It was unkind of him to say that.
sceneCN: 这里 unkind 是「刻薄的、不厚道的」（第 1 个义项：待人冷酷伤人）；句意为他那样说太不厚道。伸出的手被干脆拨开，正是这个词的核心画面。

collocations.phrase: it is unkind of someone to

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「刻薄地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「刻薄；不仁」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「善良的；和善的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「善意；亲切」

senses.title: Cruel or cold in words
senses.definition: saying things that are hard, cold, or hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 说出冷酷伤人、不近情理的话
senses.example: It was unkind to laugh at his mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑他的错误太刻薄了。
senses.why: The prefix denies kind, and kind comes from the old word for one family, so unkind is treating someone as a stranger.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 kind，而 kind 本出自「同族」的古义，所以 unkind 就是把人当作外人对待。

senses.title: Hard in action, not only in words
senses.definition: acting in a way that ignores another person trouble
senses.definitionCN: 做事时全然不顾别人的难处
senses.example: It was unkind of them to leave her standing in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把她丢在雨里站着，实在不厚道。
senses.why: Whatever denies kin denies the help kin deserve, so the word covers deeds as well as speech.
senses.whyCN: 否定「同类」也就否定了同类应得的照料，所以这个词兼指言与行。

senses.title: Chilling an atmosphere
senses.definition: used of treatment that shows no warmth or care
senses.definitionCN: 形容毫无暖意与关照的对待
senses.example: The unkind treatment she met at the front desk upset her all day.
senses.exampleCN: 她在前台受到的冷遇让她难受了一整天。
senses.why: Hard words repeated become an atmosphere, and the adjective follows them there.
senses.whyCN: 刻薄的话反复出现就成了气氛，这个形容词也随之延伸过去。

senses.title: Harsh in its effects
senses.titleCN: 苛刻的；不近人情的（评判）
senses.definition: used of a judgement or condition that shows no mercy
senses.definitionCN: 形容毫不留情的评判或处境
senses.example: The review of her first book was unkind but fair.
senses.exampleCN: 对她第一本书的评论很苛刻，却也公道。
senses.why: A judgement that considers no one feelings repeats the same lack of kin.
senses.whyCN: 不顾任何人感受的评判，重复着同样的「不认同类」。

senses.title: Against the nature of something
senses.definition: in older use, used of a climate or soil that does not suit a plant
senses.definitionCN: 较古用法，形容气候或土壤不适于某种草木
senses.example: They planted the vine where the soil was unkind to it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把葡萄种在土质不适合它生长的地方。
senses.why: Being unsuited to a plant is the same denial of kind, moved from people to soil.
senses.whyCN: 不适宜草木，仍是同一种对 kind 的否定，只是从人挪到了土壤。

intro.en: Kind is an old English word for nature and family, and the negative prefix reverses its warmth.
intro.cn: kind 是古英语中表示「天性、同族」的词，否定前缀把那份暖意反了过来。

items.en: Gecynd meant nature or race, and cynde meant natural or well-born.
items.cn: gecynd 意为天性、族类，cynde 意为本性的、出身好的。

items.en: Kind came to mean well-disposed, then warm and considerate.
items.cn: kind 转为表示「心性好的」，再变为「温和体贴的」。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to kind to name the opposite temper.
items.cn: 在 kind 前加 un-，用来命名相反的性情。

items.en: Unkind was applied first to words and looks, then to deeds.
items.cn: unkind 先用于言语神情，再扩展到行为。

items.en: The older sense survives in kind as a noun for a sort or type.
items.cn: 较古的「种类」之义仍存于名词 kind 之中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kind forms, and the near-meaning group covers cruel words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 kind 的各个形式，近义组覆盖与刻薄残忍相关的词。

entries.definition: in a warm and caring way
in a cold and hurtful way

entries.definitionCN: 放松；解开（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word denies kinship: someone who is unkind treats you as though you were not one of us.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定的是「同类」：不厚道的人把你当作外人。

normal.en: Un- plus kind: without the warmth owed to kin.
normal.cn: un- 加 kind：没有那份对同类该有的暖意。

normal.en: Be unkind to someone and it is unkind to do are the two frames.
normal.cn: be unkind to someone 与 It is unkind to do 是两个常用句型。

normal.en: Kind also means type, as in a kind of bird.
normal.cn: kind 还有「种类」之义，如 a kind of bird。

normal.en: Unkindly is the adverb, unkindness the noun.
normal.cn: 副词是 unkindly，名词是 unkindness。

normal.en: Unkind is gentler than cruel; it judges manner rather than intent.
normal.cn: unkind 比 cruel 轻，评的是态度而非蓄意伤害。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reached out that is simply brushed away.
abstract.cn: 想象伸出去的手被干脆拨开。

abstract.en: See a child told to go away in a flat voice.
abstract.cn: 看孩子被一个平板的声调赶走。

abstract.en: Hear laughter that starts before the joke ends.
abstract.cn: 听笑声在笑话结束前就先响起来。

examples.en: It was unkind to point out the mistake in front of everyone.
examples.cn: 当众指出那个错误，太不厚道。

examples.en: She never said an unkind word about her neighbours.
examples.cn: 她从没说过邻居一句刻薄话。

examples.en: He treated the new pupil unkindly at first and regretted it later.
examples.cn: 他起初对那个转学生很刻薄，后来后悔了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺砍的」——话说得像刀砍一样，一刀一刀割在人心上，太不厚道。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ kind，kind 源自古英语 cynde/gecynd（天性、族类），由「同族、本性」转义为「和善」

sensesIntro.en: One denial of kinship runs from a cold remark to a harsh review and even to unsuitable soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对「同类」的否定，从冷言冷语延伸到苛刻评论，乃至不宜的土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an offered hand brushed away.
core.cn: 核心意象：递出的手被一把拨开。

branches.en: The word branch: jokes and remarks that cut.
branches.cn: 言语分支：伤人的玩笑与话。

branches.en: The deed branch: leaving someone in the rain.
branches.cn: 行为分支：把某人丢在雨里。

branches.en: The atmosphere branch: treatment with no warmth.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：毫无暖意的对待。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a review without mercy.
branches.cn: 评判分支：毫不留情的评论。

branches.en: The natural branch: soil that does not suit a plant.
branches.cn: 自然分支：不宜草木的土壤。

intro.en: The parts are a negative prefix and a very old native adjective.
intro.cn: 部件是否定前缀与一个极古的本土形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer; kind is Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语层，kind 属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: Her kindness was remembered for years.
items.exampleCN: 她的善意被人记了很多年。

items.example: A cruel word can last a lifetime.
items.exampleCN: 一句残忍的话能记一辈子。

items.example: A thoughtless remark spoiled the evening.
items.exampleCN: 一句不体谅的话毁了这个晚上。

definition_zh: 不太可能的；未必会发生的；不大可信的；（人）不像是真的
definition_en: not probable, or hard to believe when told
core_image: 一条窄路通向高处的城堡，看着就上不去
scene: 大家都以为他考不过，可他自己偷偷每天早起做题。It is unlikely that he will fail.
sceneCN: 这里 unlikely 是「不大可能的」（第 1 个义项：发生机会小）；句意为他不太可能考不过。一条看着就上不去的窄路，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「可能的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不太可能」
由 likely 派生的名词，义为「可能性」
由 like 派生的名词，义为「相似」

senses.title: Not expected to happen
senses.definition: having little chance of happening or being true
senses.definitionCN: 发生或成立的可能性很小
senses.example: A change of plan this late seems unlikely.
senses.exampleCN: 这么晚再改计划看来不太可能。
senses.why: Like used to mean similar, and likely meant probable; removing that leaves little chance.
senses.whyCN: like 古义为「相似」，likely 意为「可能」，去掉这份相似，剩下的就是机会甚微。

senses.title: Used with a verb in the infinitive
senses.definition: used as be unlikely to plus a verb to say a thing will probably not happen
senses.definitionCN: 用作 be unlikely to 加动词，说明某事大概不会发生
senses.example: She is unlikely to arrive before ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她大概十点前到不了。
senses.why: Probability attached to a person turns into a prediction about that person actions.
senses.whyCN: 挂在人身上的「可能性」，就转成了关于此人行为的推测。

senses.title: Someone or something in the wrong place
senses.definition: used of a person or place that is surprising in a particular role
senses.definitionCN: 形容某人在某角色或某地出现得令人吃惊
senses.example: The old garage became an unlikely art gallery.
senses.exampleCN: 那间旧车库成了一个意想不到的画廊。
senses.why: A thing that does not resemble its expected role is literally unlike it.
senses.whyCN: 与预期角色不像的东西，字面上就是「不像」。

senses.title: Hard to believe when told
senses.definition: used of a story that is hard to accept as true
senses.definitionCN: 形容难以当作真事接受的叙述
senses.example: He told an unlikely story about a missed ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了个关于错过渡船的、不大可信的故事。
senses.why: What is improbable in fact is also improbable in belief, so one word serves both.
senses.whyCN: 事实上的不可能，与相信上的不可能本是同一回事，一个词就兼顾了。

senses.title: A pairing that should not work
senses.definition: used of partnerships or combinations that succeed against expectation
senses.definitionCN: 形容出人意料却奏效的搭档或组合
senses.example: Their unlikely friendship lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们这段意想不到的友谊维持了四十年。
senses.why: Two things that resemble nothing of each other should not fit, yet here they do.
senses.whyCN: 彼此毫不相像的两样东西本不该合适，这里却恰好合适。

intro.en: Likely grew from like meaning similar, and un- was added to deny probability.
intro.cn: likely 由意为「相似」的 like 发展而来，un- 则用来否定其可能性。

items.en: Gelic meant having the same form, from a Germanic root for body or form.
items.cn: gelic 意为「形态相同」，词根在日耳曼语中指形体。

items.en: Likely first meant similar in appearance, then probable.
items.cn: likely 初指外貌相似，后转为「可能的」。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to likely for what is hardly expected.
items.cn: 在 likely 前加 un-，表示几乎不会被预期的事。

items.en: Be unlikely to became a fixed pattern for predictions.
items.cn: be unlikely to 成为固定预测句型。

items.en: Unlikely also describes people and places used in surprising roles.
items.cn: unlikely 也用来形容出现在意外角色中的人与地方。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the like family, and the near-meaning group gathers probability words.
note.cn: 形近组是 like 词族，近义组汇集表示可能性的词。

entries.definitionCN: 不讨人喜欢的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word denies resemblance: if things are not alike, the chance is small.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定的是「相似」：彼此不像，机会自然就小。

normal.en: Un- plus likely: not probable.
normal.cn: un- 加 likely：不大可能。

normal.en: Be unlikely to do is the pattern to remember for predictions.
normal.cn: be unlikely to do 是预测时需要记住的句型。

normal.en: Highly unlikely is the common intensifier.
normal.cn: highly unlikely 是常用的加强说法。

normal.en: Like also means similar, which explains the root.
normal.cn: like 还有「相似」之义，这解释了它的词根。

normal.en: An unlikely hero is a favourite phrase in news writing.
normal.cn: an unlikely hero 是新闻写作中的常用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow path climbing to a castle that seems unreachable.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄路通向看似上不去的城堡。

abstract.en: See two people who share no taste in anything, laughing together.
abstract.cn: 看两个毫无共同爱好的人一起大笑。

abstract.en: Hear a weather report promise snow in June.
abstract.cn: 听天气预报说六月有雪。

examples.en: It is unlikely that the shop will open on Sunday.
examples.cn: 这家店星期天不太可能开门。

examples.en: He is unlikely to agree without reading it first.
examples.cn: 不先读一遍，他不太可能同意。

examples.en: The station became an unlikely setting for an opera.
examples.cn: 火车站成了一个意想不到的歌剧舞台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺来客利」——俺来客人了？这年月不太可能，怕是弄错了。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ likely，likely 源自古英语 gelic（形态相同），词根在日耳曼语中意为「形体」，由「相似」转义为「可能的」

sensesIntro.en: One denied resemblance covers chance, prediction, surprising roles, shaky stories, and odd pairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对「相似」的否定，覆盖几率、预测、意外的角色、可疑的故事与奇怪的组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path climbing to a castle that looks unreachable.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条通向看似上不去的城堡的窄路。

branches.en: The chance branch: little likelihood of happening.
branches.cn: 几率分支：发生的可能很小。

branches.en: The prediction branch: people unlikely to act.
branches.cn: 预测分支：人们不太会做的事。

branches.en: The setting branch: a person or place in the wrong role.
branches.cn: 场景分支：出现在意料之外角色里的人或地。

branches.en: The belief branch: a story that will not convince.
branches.cn: 相信分支：说服不了人的叙述。

branches.en: The pairing branch: a match that should not work.
branches.cn: 组合分支：本不该合适的搭配。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective that came from an old word for likeness.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个源自「相似」古词的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 想法相近的人所见略同。
like 加 un- 成为 unlike，意为不同。

items.example: An improbable win is still a win.
items.exampleCN: 不太可能的胜利也是胜利。

items.example: An implausible excuse convinced no one.
items.exampleCN: 一个难以信服的理由没能说服人。

items.example: It is doubtful the plan will work.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划能否奏效值得怀疑。

definition_zh: 不幸的；倒霉的；不吉利的；不凑巧的
definition_en: having bad luck, or believed to bring bad luck
core_image: 刚打出的一手好牌，最后却被人一分反超
scene: 他赶到车站时，车刚刚开走，地面上还留着轮印。He was unlucky to miss the last train.
sceneCN: 这里 unlucky 是「倒霉的」（第 1 个义项：运气不好）；句意为他赶上末班车算是运气不好。好牌却被反超，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不幸地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不幸；倒霉」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「幸运的」
词族核心名词，义为「运气」

senses.title: Hit by bad luck
senses.definition: suffering from bad luck that no one could have prevented
senses.definitionCN: 碰上谁都避免不了的不顺
senses.example: He was unlucky to lose on the last point.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分上输了，实在倒霉。
senses.why: The prefix negates lucky, and luck came into English from Dutch as a word for chance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 lucky，而 luck 由荷兰语进入英语，本指机遇。

senses.title: In an unlucky situation
senses.definition: used with in to describe a field where luck has gone against someone
senses.definitionCN: 与 in 连用，说明某方面运气不济
senses.example: He has always been unlucky in business.
senses.exampleCN: 他做生意一直运气不佳。
senses.why: Chance can favour one part of life and betray another, which the phrase with in marks.
senses.whyCN: 机遇会偏爱生活的某一方面而背弃另一面，与 in 连用正标记这一点。

senses.title: Bad luck at the wrong moment
senses.definition: used of a small accident of timing that spoils a plan
senses.definitionCN: 形容恰好毁掉计划的小小时间差
senses.example: An unlucky step sent the tray to the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 脚下不凑巧一步，托盘就摔到了地上。
senses.why: Small accidents are the smallest pieces of chance, and the word covers them too.
senses.whyCN: 小意外是机遇最小的碎片，这个词同样涵盖。

senses.title: Believed to bring bad fortune
senses.definition: used of numbers, days, or objects that people think carry bad luck
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们认为带着厄运的数字、日子或器物
senses.example: In many buildings the unlucky floor number is left out.
senses.exampleCN: 许多楼里会跳过那个不吉利的楼层号。
senses.why: From bad luck that happens to bad luck that is said to come, the word widens its reach.
senses.whyCN: 从「碰上的坏运」到「据说会来的坏运」，这个词扩大了应用范围。

senses.title: A person who deserves sympathy
senses.definition: used of someone whose bad luck is not their own fault
senses.definitionCN: 形容运气不佳而非自作自受的人
senses.example: The unlucky passengers queued again for the next flight.
senses.exampleCN: 那些倒霉的乘客又排队等下一班飞机。
senses.why: Chance strikes without blame, and the word often carries a note of sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 机遇的打击无关过错，因此这个词常带着同情的意味。

intro.en: Luck entered English from Low German or Dutch in the sixteenth century, and unlucky followed.
intro.cn: luck 十六世纪由低地德语或荷兰语进入英语，unlucky 随之出现。

items.en: Luc or luk meant good fortune in the gambling sense.
items.cn: luc 或 luk 在赌博语境中意为好运。

items.en: English borrowed luck and quickly used it for chance in general.
items.cn: 英语借入 luck，很快用来泛指机遇。

items.en: Unlucky was formed by adding the negative prefix to lucky.
items.cn: lucky 加否定前缀形成 unlucky。

items.en: The word extended to numbers, days, and objects thought to bring harm.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到被认为招祸的数字、日子与器物。

items.en: It remains the everyday word for a chance victim.
items.cn: 至今它仍指被机运击中的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers luck words, and the near-meaning group covers misfortune words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 luck 词族，近义组覆盖表示不幸的词。

entries.definitionCN: 不太可能的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: One prefix denies luck, and the word runs from a lost point to a number nobody prints.
normalIntro.cn: 一个前缀否定了运气，从丢的一分一直到没人印出的数字。

normal.en: Un- plus lucky: not favoured by chance.
normal.cn: un- 加 lucky：没被机遇眷顾。

normal.en: Be unlucky to do is the pattern for bad breaks.
normal.cn: be unlucky to do 是形容倒霉事的常用句型。

normal.en: Unlucky in love is a fixed phrase with in.
normal.cn: unlucky in love 是与 in 连用的固定说法。

normal.en: Luck came from Dutch, so it is not a Latin word.
normal.cn: luck 来自荷兰语，并不是拉丁语词。

normal.en: Unluckily is the adverb; unfortunately is more formal.
normal.cn: 副词是 unluckily，unfortunately 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a good hand of cards beaten by one point.
abstract.cn: 想象一手好牌被一分反超。

abstract.en: See a train leaving as you reach the platform.
abstract.cn: 看火车在你跑上站台时开走。

abstract.en: See a lift panel with one number missing.
abstract.cn: 看电梯按钮上缺了一个数字。

examples.en: The unlucky driver was hit from behind twice in one week.
examples.cn: 那位倒霉的司机一周里被追尾两次。

examples.en: Thirteen is thought unlucky in some countries.
examples.cn: 十三个一些国家被认为不吉利。

examples.en: Unluckily, the rain began exactly at the ceremony.
examples.cn: 不幸的是，雨恰好在仪式开始时下了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺落地记」——俺一落地就挨记一下，走了才有脚印，真倒霉。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ lucky，luck 于十六世纪自低地德语或荷兰语 luc/luk（好运）进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One denial of chance covers a lost match, a wrong moment, a forbidden number, and a sympathetically late passenger.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对机遇的否定，覆盖输掉的比赛、错的时刻、被忌讳的数字与令人同情的晚到乘客。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong hand beaten by a single point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一手好牌被一分反超。

branches.en: The break branch: losing on the last point.
branches.cn: 运气分支：在最后一分上输掉。

branches.en: The life-area branch: luck that fails in one field.
branches.cn: 生活领域分支：某一方面运气不济。

branches.en: The timing branch: a step taken half a second early.
branches.cn: 时机分支：早了半秒的一步。

branches.en: The omen branch: numbers and days said to bring harm.
branches.cn: 预兆分支：据说招祸的数字与日子。

branches.en: The sympathy branch: the passenger who did nothing wrong.
branches.cn: 同情分支：毫无过错的乘客。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective that English borrowed from Dutch.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个借自荷兰语的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: Luck is not Latin, so the Latin list is empty for this word.
latinIntro.cn: luck 并非拉丁语词，因此这个词的拉丁词条留空。

items.example: An ill-fated voyage lost three ships.
items.exampleCN: 一次注定不祥的航行失了三艘船。

items.example: The plan was doomed from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这计划从一开始就注定失败。
